Wider Sports News.title: Will shift to self-improvement brand save Enhanced Games after ‘Steroid Olympics’ lacklustre debut?
Wider Sports News.summary: After years of hype, the inaugural Enhanced Games produced mediocre performances, limited audience interest and a US$62 million loss for its parent company. But with its backers eager to tap into the ‘self-optimisation’ market, is it still a long-term threat to the anti-doping movement? The post Will shift to self-improvement brand save Enhanced Games after ‘Steroid Olympics’ lacklustre debut? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The Enhanced Games were the most radical and controversial experiment of the sporting year. To many, its sporting and commercial results have looked underwhelming. The brainchild of Australian businessman Aron D’Souza, the Enhanced Games were co-founded as a business venture by German biotech billionaire Christian Angermayer and tech investment banker turned crypto entrepreneur Maximillian Martin.

They secured backing in tech and libertarian spaces through the likes of Peter Thiel and 1789 Capital, an ‘anti-ESG’ VC firm whose partners include Donald Trump Jr. The initial premise was simple: a sporting event which lifted competitive restrictions on doping and equipment to push athletic performance beyond its natural limits. Tapping into decades of fatalism around the use of drugs in sport, the concept was widely – and not always pejoratively – dubbed the ‘Steroid Olympics’.

Wider Sports News.title: Cancelled events, unpaid bills and uncertain vision: Will LIV Golf survive PIF’s exit?
Wider Sports News.summary: After the sudden withdrawal of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, LIV Golf has endured a tumultuous 2026. The once free-spending tour has cut prize purses, missed payments to contractors, and ended its season a week early. But with a new investor lined up, the LIV leadership remain confident of finding a new place in the sport. The post Cancelled events, unpaid bills and uncertain vision: Will LIV Golf survive PIF’s exit? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The tour that once trumpeted itself as ‘golf, but louder’ is making a quiet exit – for 2026, at least. The final season of LIV Golf in its original form is ending early at LIV Golf Indianapolis. A planned late August finale at the Team Championship in Michigan was called off, with steep budget cuts following the withdrawal of support from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

That decision was announced back in April, when all parties indicated that funding would continue through the 2026 campaign. The Michigan cancellation, however, is just one hint that life after PIF has already begun.

Wider Sports News.body:
AD Ports Group, the integrated port, logistics chain and free zone operator, has hired HSBC to advise on a planned takeover bid by Abu Dhabi sovereign investment arm L’imad. The company’s board, which met through video conferencing, discussed the potential bid and “resolved to approve the appointment of HSBC Bank Middle East as the company’s financial advisers to oversee the transaction”, it said in a statement to Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, where its shares are traded.

The company offered no indication of a deadline for the transaction. L'imad this week announced it would bid to acquire 100 per cent of the AD Ports Group shares it does not already own, to expand its logistics portfolio.

Wider Sports News.title: Olympic champion Alistair Brownlee: ‘Triathlon incredibly healthy but probably needs consolidation’
Wider Sports News.summary: Two-time gold medal winner praises investment in the sport as World Triathlon moves to create centralised tour. The post Olympic champion Alistair Brownlee: ‘Triathlon incredibly healthy but probably needs consolidation’ appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Two-time Olympic triathlon champion Alistair Brownlee believes the sport is in an incredibly healthy position but thinks that greater consolidation may be needed. Triathlon was admitted to the Olympic Games in 2000, a development which catalysed participation levels and, more recently, has led to the creation of several major competitions and significant private investment.

These include SuperTri and the Professional Triathletes Organisation (PTO), which have joined the most established Ironman and World Triathlon circuits. However, apart from World Triathlon’s events, which include the Olympic competitions, all of these are privately run with varying levels of official recognition from the world governing body.

Wider Sports News.summary: English soccer’s top flight remains in a commercial league of its own, but the 2026/27 Premier League season will herald a series of changes that could have a longer-term impact on its business. The post US$7bn team valuations, a streaming pilot and sponsor overhaul: The business of the 2026/27 Premier League season appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Barely a month after Spain lifted the Fifa World Cup at MetLife Stadium in New York, the Premier League returns this week after a summer that saw 182 of its players compete at soccer’s flagship international tournament.

Players have gradually been returning to their clubs for what represents the latest-ever start to a Premier League season, a delay largely driven by the expansion of the World Cup and the wider impact Fifa’s encroachment on the calendar has had on both scheduling and player welfare.

Rugby.title: The end is in sight as Louis Bielle-Biarrey plots his future
Rugby.summary: French superstar winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey is closing in on a two-year contract extension with Bordeaux-Bègles that will keep him at the club until the summer of 2029.
Rugby.body:
French superstar winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey is closing in on a two-year contract extension with Bordeaux-Bègles that will keep him at the club until the summer of 2029. Bielle-Biarrey, 23, has scored 29 tries in 27 appearances for Les Bleus and been named Player of the Tournament in each of the last two Six Nations after helping France secure back-to-back titles.

He entered the final year of his current agreement in July and has been in talks with Bordeaux president Laurent Marti for weeks in a bid to reach a new agreement. Although he wasn’t likely to leave, minor details, including his Adidas deal, have taken time to iron out. The latest reports from France suggest the end is now in sight.

Rugby.summary: Johann van Graan begins his fifth term of office at The Rec without two of the standout performers of his reign in charge - Thomas du Toit and Alfie Barbeary.

Compared to the past two seasons, which resulted in a first league trophy in 29 years and a title defence that fell just short, Bath supporters’ confidence is not as high as it once was entering the new campaign, despite the bookies marking them down as marginal favourites ahead of reigning champions Northampton.

Johann van Graan begins his fifth term of office at The Rec without two standout performers – Thomas du Toit and Alfie Barbeary – and with a new attack coach, albeit someone very familiar to both him and chief playmaker, Finn Russell, in ex-Munster man Mike Prendergast.

Rugby.title: 'South Africa have the All Blacks right where they want them'
Rugby.summary: The Springboks lost the first Test convincingly, but adversity seems to compel Rassie Erasmus' world champions to greater heights.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have made a terrible mistake. They have beaten the Springboks. Win a VIP match experience at the Baltimore Test, plus travel & accommodation up to $2,500. Worse, they have beaten them convincingly enough to ensure every South African player, coach and supporter will spend every minute until Saturday’s kick-off thinking about little else. The score was 33-16. New Zealand scored five tries to South Africa’s one. The Boks lost their world number one ranking, their 12-match winning streak and the first Test of a four-match series.

In other words, Rassie Erasmus and his players are exactly where they want to be. The Springboks are at their most dangerous when they are unhappy. They need to feel aggrieved. They need a problem. They need to believe the outside world has reached a premature conclusion about them. The All Blacks have just provided all three.

Rugby.title: 'We felt the pressure': Cobus Reinach flags All Blacks tactics
Rugby.summary: South Africa scrum-half Cobus Reinach has admitted that his side "felt the pressure" the All Blacks exerted as they fell 33-16 in the first Test of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
South Africa scrum-half Cobus Reinach has admitted that his side “felt the pressure” the All Blacks exerted as they fell 33-16 in the first Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

The veteran scrum-half, who will start this week in Cape Town after coming on from the bench at Ellis Park, spoke specifically about the way Dave Rennie’s side attacked the breakdown, with both Reinach and Grant Williams, whom he replaced, harassed by the All Blacks forwards all match.

Rugby.summary: The former England fly-half is back at the club where he had two spells as a player after being appointed as the Tigers' kicking coach.
Rugby.body:
Former England fly-half Freddie Burns has returned to Leicester, where he had two spells as a player, after being appointed as the club’s kicking coach. Leicester’s 2022 PREM-winning hero hung up his boots at the end of last season, having seen out his career in Romania, and has been given a full-time contract.

He is the second former Tigers player to join the coaching team in the space of just over a week, after Craig Newby was brought on board as the club’s part-time forwards skills coach.

Rugby.summary: Wallabies backrower Tom Hooper played 24 games for club and country last season before linking up with the Exeter Chiefs.
Rugby.body:
Wallabies backrower Tom Hooper played 24 games for club and country last season before linking up with the Exeter Chiefs, going on to make more than 20 appearances. ‘Hoops’ returned to the Wallabies fold in July, but then injury struck – only it proved to be “a blessing in disguise.”

Hooper made a 12-minute cameo off the bench in a 33-31 defeat to Ireland in Sydney, but the loose forward would take no further part in the July Tests. The Wallabies confirmed the following week that Hooper had picked up a shoulder injury.

Rugby.body:

SA Rugby mag reported a three-to-six-month recovery timeline for a syndesmosis injury. After surgery in June, the No.10 was back playing in just 10 weeks. From three months down to two and a half, ahead of the biggest series of his career.

Rugby.body:
Wallabies fly-half Ben Donaldson has stressed the importance of each match as the Aussies build towards Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 at home, describing the upcoming two-Test series away to Argentina as “vital” for the group.

The Wallabies kick off their home World Cup in a little over 13 months’ time, when they take on tournament debutants Hong Kong China in Perth on October 1. They will then face rivals the All Blacks in Sydney and Chile at Brisbane’s Suncorp Stadium.

Rugby.summary: Former number one Major League Rugby Draft pick Will Sherman has taken up an opportunity in Japan.
Rugby.body:
Former number one Major League Rugby Draft pick Will Sherman has taken up an opportunity in Japan, with the UCLA product unveiled alongside a former All Black as some of the players joining the Red Hurricanes Osaka.

Rugby.title: Three Vikes named to Canada’s FISU World University Championship Rugby Sevens team
Rugby.summary: Three Vikes named to Canada’s FISU World University Championship Rugby Sevens team University of Victoria Athletics
Rugby.body:
have been named to Canada's women's team for the 2026 FISU World University Championship Rugby Sevens. The championship will take place Sept. 4-6 in Stellenbosch, South Africa, with Canada looking to build on its silver-medal performance at the 2024 championship in Aix-en-Provence, France.

The Canadian women have a strong history at the event, winning three world university titles since rugby sevens joined the FISU World University Championship program in 2004. The 2026 Canadian squad features student-athletes from 10 universities across Canada and the United States, including three representatives from UVic.

Rugby.title: Dave Rennie's verdict on bruising Timoci Tavatavanawai All Blacks performance
Rugby.summary: It was a night of linebreaks and freestyle rugby at Ellis Park on Tuesday, with the All Blacks completing a wild comeback against a Lions team that outperformed expectations in front of a vocal Johannesburg crowd.
Rugby.body:
It was a night of linebreaks and freestyle rugby at Ellis Park on Tuesday, with the All Blacks completing a wild comeback against a Lions team that outperformed expectations in front of a vocal Johannesburg crowd.

Starring in the performance was powerful All Blacks midfielder Timoci Tavatavanawai, who led the game with eight tackle busts on 13 carries, while making three linebreaks, running for 137 metres with the ball in hand, winning two steals, and making four offloads.

Rugby.title: 'Grit and guts': Rieko Ioane on scratchy All Blacks victory over Lions
Rugby.summary: "This is my third time playing this Lions team, and I sort of knew coming into this game that they were probably the least affected by in terms of international selection.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks outside-back Rieko Ioane has reflected on what was a patchy team performance against the Lions at Ellis Park in Johannesburg. The All Blacks’ last midweek clash didn’t go exactly to plan, but Ioane and other experienced players helped Dave Rennie’s side overcome a powerful Lions team at their home stadium.

The Kiwis needed impact from Xavier Numia, Bradley Slater, Saula Ma’u, and Jamie Hannah to secure the midweek victory, after a slow start by Rennie’s men. The Blues midfielder crossed twice during the second-half comeback by the All Blacks, picking off an intercept in the 55th minute. His first of the evening was from a Beauden Barrett tip-on pass, putting Ioane through a huge gap in the Lions’ defence.

Rugby.title: All Blacks coach gives injury update, loose-forward ruled out of tour
Rugby.summary: "Our feeling is now that we're beyond the midweek games; we've got enough loose forwards to pick from."
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has revealed that German-born loose-forward Anton Segner will play no further part in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour. Segner, who was ruled out of the All Blacks’ first Test against the Springboks at Ellis Park, required small keyhole surgery on his ankle.

The Blues loose-forward was named on the bench for last weekend’s clash against the Springboks, but was replaced by Chiefs No.6 Simon Parker on gameday. Rennie confirmed the news in his post-match press conference in Johannesburg, after the All Blacks’ 41-35 victory over the Lions.

Rugby.title: Burns returns to Tigers in coaching role
Rugby.summary: Former England and Leicester Tigers fly-half Freddie Burns returns to the Prem club as kicking coach.
Rugby.body:
Former England and Leicester Tigers fly-half Freddie Burns has returned to the Prem club as kicking coach. The 36-year-old landed one of the most famous kicks in the club's history when he slotted a last-minute drop-goal against Saracens to seal Tigers' 2022 Premiership title victory at Twickenham.

Burns' move into coaching with his former club comes just three weeks after he announced his retirement as a professional player. The playmaker, who was capped five times for England between 2012 and 2014, had two spells with Tigers in an eclectic career in which he also featured for Gloucester and Bath, as well as sides in New Zealand and Japan before seeing out his career as a player-coach in Romania with Dinamo Bucuresti.

Rugby.title: Canada's Pacific Nations Cup squad missing experienced French-based trio
Rugby.summary: Head coach Steve Meehan has named five uncapped players in Jamie Armstrong, Bryce Worden, Sam Turner, Ryan Cozens and Jack Gore, the Candian University Rookie of the Year in 2025.
Rugby.body:
Canada’s squad for the upcoming September Test window is missing three experienced players – hooker Andrew Quattrin, lock Evan Olmstead and No.8 Tyler Ardron. The trio, who boast 109 caps between them, are unavailable for selection for the trip to Japan, which involves a one-off fixture against the Brave Blossoms followed by two games in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup, because of their club commitments in France.

Ardron and Olmstead are at the beginning of new careers with Provence and Nice, with the Pro D2 season only a couple of days away, while Quattrin’s season with Nationale outfit Carcassonne, who he joined from Valence, is already up and running.

Rugby.title: All Blacks' latest injury replacement withdrawn from Lions game with illness
Rugby.summary: Ofa Tu'ungafasi's All Blacks return has hit a snag, with the veteran prop coming down with an illness quickly after landing in South Africa.
Rugby.body:
Ofa Tu’ungafasi’s All Blacks return has hit a snag, with the veteran prop coming down with an illness quickly after landing in South Africa. The 34-year-old only arrived in the country on Monday morning, getting a late call-up after Ethan de Groot suffered a concussion in Saturday’s 33-16 win over the Springboks. He was immediately named by Dave Rennie in the No.17 jersey in Tuesday evening’s match against the Lions. His withdrawal means Xavier Numia will come onto the All Blacks’ bench.

Tu’ungafasi hasn’t been seen in black since 2024’s northern tour, before a neck injury derailed his 2025. With the change, New Zealand’s reserve front row loses 66 Tests of experience.

Rugby.title: ProD2 season 2026-27 preview: Club-by-club guide as French second tier kicks off
Rugby.summary: With squad overhauls and coaching changes, how will all 16 teams fare heading into a new campaign in France's second tier?
Rugby.body:
Some 83 days after Vannes beat Provence in Toulouse to win promotion to the Top 14 as ProD2 champions, and 75 after Provence lost their second chance to join the Breton side in the top flight, the ProD2 returns for the 2026-27 campaign on this final Thursday in August.

Between the 16 teams and their primary target – the end of the regular season – in mid-May, are 240 matches. Or, to put it another way, 30 each. The top six will move forward to a knockout play-off race, playing between one and three more matches each. The eventual champions will be promoted to the Top 14, taking the place of the side that finishes bottom of that league. The losing ProD2 finalists then host the 13th-placed side in the Top 14 in a promotion-relegation play-off.

Rugby.title: Saracens land title-winning back after exit from London rivals
Rugby.summary: JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby champions Saracens have signed Beth Wilcock after her departure from Harlequins.
Rugby.body:
JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby champions Saracens have signed Beth Wilcock after her departure from Harlequins. Before crossing the London divide, the versatile back spent seven seasons at the Twickenham Stoop and won the Premier 15s with the club in 2021.

Last season the 25-year-old scored four tries in 14 league appearances for Harlequins as Ross Chisholm’s side missed out on play-off rugby by four points. Wilcock is one of 26 players to have departed the West Londoners this summer.

Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers have teased on social media that they will be making an announcement at 7.30 pm this evening, and it didn’t take long for social media sleuths to work out it’s likely to be Freddie Burns returning to Welford Road as kicking coach.
Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers have teased on social media that they will be making an announcement at 7.30 pm this evening, and it didn’t take long for social media sleuths to work out it’s likely to be Freddie Burns returning to Welford Road as kicking coach.

The club posted footage on X of an arm hanging up a pair of boots on a dressing room hook before picking up a baseball cap, and fans soon worked out the boots were Adidas Predators, similar to the type Burns used to land a PREM title-winning drop goal.

Rugby.title: Siya Kolisi declared fit to face All Blacks with Pieter-Steph du Toit decision reversed
Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus has confirmed that Siya Kolisi will start and captain South Africa against the All Blacks in Cape Town on Saturday after successfully coming through the final stages of his return from a hamstring injury.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus has confirmed that Siya Kolisi will start and captain South Africa against the All Blacks in Cape Town on Saturday after successfully coming through the final stages of his return from a hamstring injury.

Kolisi was initially bracketed with Paul de Villiers when Erasmus named his side on Monday, with the Springbok coaches giving the 104-cap flanker additional time to prove his fitness. Pieter-Steph du Toit was consequently announced as captain for what will be his 100th Test.

Rugby.title: Loughborough announce temporary coaching shake-up ahead of Lightning season
Rugby.summary: Loughborough Lightning head coach Nathan Smith will spend the WXV Global Series campaign with Canada.
Rugby.body:
Loughborough Lightning head coach Nathan Smith will spend the WXV Global Series campaign on secondment with Canada. Between September and October, Lightning assistant coach Rachel Taylor will lead the East Midlands club in their JAECOO PWR Next Gen Cup fixtures against Sale Sharks, Saracens, Exeter Chiefs and Leicester Tigers.

Former Wales captain, Taylor, was previously head coach of Sale Sharks before she joined Loughborough as an assistant coach in 2025. Smith was preciously seconded to Kévin Rouet’s coaching staff with Canada for this year’s Pacific Four Series campaign, where he led the team’s lineout.

Rugby.summary: With the Pro D2 starting this Thursday, French media outlet Midi Olympique has revealed the budgets of each one of the 16 sides competing in the 2026/2027 season.
Rugby.body:
With the Pro D2 starting this Thursday, French media outlet Midi Olympique has revealed the budgets of each one of the 16 sides competing in the 2026/2027 season. Philippe Saint-André’s Provence, who came close to clinching promotion to the Top 14 a few months ago, boasts a €20m budget, the biggest amongst the ProD2 landscape.

The 2025/2026 runners-up have signed the likes of Canadian legend Tyler Ardron, Martín Bogado, Fijian Drua’s Etonia Waqa and former Castres’ prop Aurélien Azar in hopes of winning promotion to the Top 14 for the first time in their history.

Rugby.title: Newcastle sign Pumas prop Moreno
Rugby.summary: Argentina prop Francisco Moreno joins Newcastle Red Bulls, signing a one-year deal with the Prem outfit.
Rugby.body:
Argentina prop Francisco Moreno has become the latest international to join Newcastle Red Bulls, signing a one-year deal with the Prem outfit. The 24-year-old tight-head made his Test debut for Los Pumas against world champions South Africa earlier this month and is currently with the national side preparing for Saturday's match against Australia.

He will join up with Pumas team-mates Franco Molina and Simon Benitez Cruz on Tyneside following the end of his international commitments. Moreno becomes the 25th signing for the Red Bulls as they refresh a side that finished bottom of the Prem table in 2025-26 season with just two wins.

Rugby.title: Dual-code legend and Welsh sporting icon Sir Billy Boston dies, aged 92
Rugby.summary: Boston scored 571 tries in 562 games, helping Great Britain win the World Cup in 1960 and three Challenge Cups after switching codes.
Rugby.body:
Sir Billy Boston, “one of the best-loved and most iconic figures in the history of Welsh sport”, has died in hospital in Wigan, aged 92, just four days after the funeral of his wife of 70 years, Lady Joan.

Boston scored 571 tries in 562 games, helping Great Britain win the World Cup in 1960 and three Challenge Cups after switching codes when his dreams of playing for Cardiff and Wales were dashed because he was black.

Rugby.summary: Legendary All Blacks fly-half Dan Carter has described South Africa No.10 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu as a "rare talent", but has said "you don't become a world-class first five overnight by having two or three good seasons."
Rugby.body:
Legendary All Blacks fly-half Dan Carter has described South Africa No.10 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu as a “rare talent”, but has said “you don’t become a world-class first five overnight by having two or three good seasons.”

The 44-year-old Kiwi gave his verdict on the Springboks playmaker when joining the For The Love Of Rugby: South Africa podcast recently, where he revealed that the 24-year-old had reached out to him for advice.

Rugby.title: Sakura Fifteen turn to 43-cap Brave Blossoms lock as new head coach
Rugby.summary: 43-cap Brave Blossoms lock Toshizumi Kitagawa has been appointed as head coach of the Sakura Fifteen ahead of the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
43-cap Brave Blossoms lock Toshizumi Kitagawa has been appointed as head coach of the Sakura Fifteen ahead of the WXV Global Series. This September, Japan will play Italy and Ireland in Europe, before hosting Wales for two Tests on home soil in October. They will also play Ireland once outside of the WXV Global Series window.

Kitagawa represented the Japan men’s national team between 2005 and 2013, and represented his country at the 2011 Rugby World Cup in New Zealand. During his professional playing career, Kitagawa represented Toyota Verblitz for 15 years before he concluded his time on the pitch with Hino Red Dolphins, who he then worked for as an assistant coach between 2021 and 2023.

Rugby.title: Daddy of all Springboks: Deon Fourie to join list of world's oldest internationals
Rugby.summary: One month shy of his 40th birthday, versatile Stormers forward Deon Fourie is set to become the oldest player to play for the Springboks.
Rugby.body:
One month shy of his 40th birthday, versatile Stormers forward Deon Fourie is set to become the oldest player to play for the Springboks. Named on the bench for the second Test against New Zealand in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, Fourie will be 39 years and 338 days old on Saturday, beating the record previously held by Victor Matfield if he is pressed into action in Cape Town.

Matfield made the last of his 127 appearances for South Africa in the semi-final of RWC 2015, aged 38 years and 172 days, a record that has stood the test of time since then, although Schalk Brits (38 years, 145 days) came close in 2019.

Rugby.title: 'That was interesting with Rassie, something you don't often see': Victor Matfield
Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has highlighted the difference between the two benches in the All Blacks' 33-16 win over the Springboks at Ellis Park on Saturday, saying “we didn't see the impact of the Bomb Squad for the first time” in the first Test of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry.
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has highlighted the difference between the two benches in the All Blacks‘ 33-16 win over the Springboks at Ellis Park on Saturday, saying “we didn’t see the impact of the Bomb Squad for the first time” in the first Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

New Zealand won the second half in Johannesburg 21-3, with six of South Africa’s eight substitutes failing to see their side score a point while they were on the field. After experiencing initial success in the scrum, loosehead Gerhard Steenekamp was taken off 20 minutes after coming on for Jan-Hendrik Wessels. Likewise, despite scoring a try after replacing Kurt-Lee Arendse in the first half, Andre Esterhuizen was replaced in the second half.

Rugby.title: Bristol sign ex-Tigers lock Wells on three-month deal
Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears sign former Leicester Tigers lock Harry Wells on a three-month deal.
Rugby.body:
Bristol Bears have signed former Leicester Tigers lock Harry Wells on a short-term deal. The 32-year-old spent more than a decade with the Tigers and was part of the side that won the Premiership title at Twickenham in 2022 and last season's Prem Rugby Cup.

The experienced forward, who can operate across the second row and back row, made 236 appearances for Leicester and has joined Bears from fourth-tier side Oundle on a three-month deal.

Rugby.title: Ex-Leicester lock Harry Wells returns to the PREM on short-term deal
Rugby.summary: Experienced lock Harry Wells has joined Bristol Bears on a three-month deal ahead of the 2026/27 season.
Rugby.body:
Experienced loose forward Harry Wells has joined Bristol Bears on a three-month deal ahead of the 2026/27 season. The 32-year-old arrives at the Bears with a wealth of Gallagher PREM and Investec Champions Cup experience following more than a decade at Leicester Tigers, where he made 236 first-team appearances after progressing through the club’s Academy.

Wells made his Tigers debut as a 19-year-old in 2013 before returning to Welford Road as a senior player in 2016 following a spell with Bedford Blues in the Championship. A Gallagher PREM winner in 2022, he was released by Leicester at the end of last season and signed for ambitious National 2 East outfit, Oundle RFC, as a player-coach, who have agreed to release Wells for the duration of the short-term deal with the Bears.

Rugby.title: Uruguay turn to former Rugby World Cup coach to lead them into new era
Rugby.summary: Uruguay have unveiled Guzmán Barreiro as head coach of Los Teros, with the former High Performance director replacing Argentinian Rodolfo Ambrósio in the role.
Rugby.body:
Uruguay have unveiled Guzmán Barreiro as head coach of Los Teros, with the former High Performance director replacing Argentinian Rodolfo Ambrósio in the role. With one year to go before the next Rugby World Cup, the Uruguayan Rugby Union made significant changes to the coaching staff, entrusting Barreiro with full control over assembling a staff that reflects his vision for the national team.

Barreiro’s senior coaching career began in the early 2010s, when he joined Montevideo’s Old Christians Club, leading the club to three national titles before joining the union in 2016 as an assistant coach of Esteban Meneses team.

Rugby.title: Mike Blair: 'We've got so much growth in us, there's more we can do'
Rugby.summary: "We're really pleased with five tries, I was just being to Jordie Barrett there, and I was saying to him like, there's there's so much good stuff there, but the exciting bit is we've got so much growth in us," Blair said on Sky Sport.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach and former Scotland halfback Mike Blair believes his side are yet to reach full potential, insisting they have more to give with ball in hand. Blair’s admission follows the All Blacks’ impressive five-tries-to-one victory in front of 60 thousand fans at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, where Dave Rennie’s side came from behind at halftime to clinch the first Test match of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series for 2026.

The 45-year-old, who joined the All Blacks coaching staff as an attack coach, has been in the role for only five months, but has clearly made an impact with a new attacking blueprint on display.

Rugby.title: ‘The closest I ever got’: NRL great reveals All Blacks Sevens talks
Rugby.summary: Former NZ Warriors halfback Shaun Johnson could’ve made a shock switch away from the NRL to play for the All Blacks Sevens.
Rugby.body:
Former NZ Warriors halfback Shaun Johnson could’ve made a shock switch away from the NRL to play for the All Blacks Sevens, revealing how close he came to leaving the code during the prime of his decorated career.

Johnson helped the Warriors reach the 2011 NRL Grand Final as a rookie, featuring in the same run-on side as utility back Krisnan Inu, who later spent some time in France’s Top 14 with Parisian side Stade Francais.

Rugby.title: ‘Not just a pipe dream’: How a social media star fared against some Wallabies
Rugby.summary: Tiarnan Neville became the first person to slot the Celebrity First Kick! at Nudgee College earlier this month.
Rugby.body:
Tiarnan Neville became the first person to slot the Celebrity First Kick! at Nudgee College earlier this month, with the social media sensation coolly sending the attempt between the sticks from near the left sideline on the 22.

Neville has built a strong following on TikTok and Instagram, with more than 39,000 followers on both platforms, while playing the sport around the world. The 25-year-old nailed the kick in front of cheering Nudgee students, before a Wallabies great stepped up to do the same.

Rugby.title: You don't pick Handre Pollard to score tries
Rugby.summary: Despite the idea that Erasmus keeps everyone second guessing, the repeated patterns in team naming and selection make the Springboks a predictable side.
Rugby.body:
Despite the idea that Erasmus keeps everyone second guessing, the repeated patterns in team naming and selection make the Springboks fairly predictable. We know that Erasmus has the team planned out for every Test in the entire series, with mass changes due despite the result. After a loss, it is almost certain they will stick to the pre-planned teams and rotate out. The only uncertainty is when injuries strike, which on this occasion have forced Cheslin Kolbe out of the side for the second Test.

We even know how they will play in Cape Town. You don’t pick Handre Pollard to score tries. Even more so when they guy he replaced, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, is South Africa’s most talented N0.10 in generations.

Rugby.summary: Fabian Holland has picked up where he left off in the black jersey, returning from a six-month stint on the sidelines to play a crucial role in the All Blacks' dramatic win over the Springboks in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test series opener.
Rugby.body:
Fabian Holland has picked up where he left off in the black jersey, returning from a six-month stint on the sidelines to play a crucial role in the All Blacks‘ dramatic win over the Springboks in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series opener.

Fresh off a World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year award in 2025, the towering Highlanders lock lasted just a few minutes in his first pre-season game of 2026, picking up a shoulder injury that would then see him miss the entire Super Rugby Pacific campaign.

Rugby.title: 'Poked a bear': Neil Barnes on the Springboks' response awaiting the All Blacks
Rugby.summary: The Kiwis, who head into the second Test match with seven wins from seven games in 2026, are preparing for a Springboks bounce-back performance, according to Barnes.
Rugby.body:
Straight-shooting All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes has no illusions about the Springboks’ motivation heading into the second Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry. Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks will take on the All Blacks in Cape Town after falling to their first defeat since Eden Park in 2025, winning twelve Tests in between the two contests with the Kiwis.

But the All Blacks, under new head coach Dave Rennie, rocked up to Ellis Park and took home the chocolates, claiming their biggest winning margin over the Springboks at the storied ground.

Jemima Adams-Verling, Sophie Barrett, Beth Buttimer, Caitríona Finn, Kate Jordan, Lucia Linn and Alana McInerney are all yet to win their maiden Ireland caps, but have impressed in Celtic Challenge and Vodafone Women’s Interprovincial Championship action.

Rugby.title: Springboks concede famous bench tactic finally 'backfired' against All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has conceded that his famous 6/2 bench tactic "backfired" on his team against the All Blacks in Johannesburg, and it was an avoidable mistake.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has conceded that his famous 6/2 bench tactic “backfired” on his team against the All Blacks at Ellis Park, and it was an avoidable mistake.

South Africa, famous for their physical forward pack, opted to double down on that strength for game one of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series, stacking their bench with six forwards and just two backs as opposed to the traditional five forwards and three backs, which provides more even cover in the event of injury.

Rugby.title: Spencer to miss start of Bath's season after surgery
Rugby.summary: Bath captain Ben Spencer will miss the start of the 2026-27 season but Will Stuart and Jaco Coetzee among those returning.
Rugby.body:
Bath captain and England scrum-half Ben Spencer will miss the opening weeks of the 2026-27 Prem season after having surgery on a long-standing shoulder injury. The 34-year-old missed two games for Bath in April after he injured his shoulder; however, he returned to conclude the season and was part of England's squad this summer for the Nations Championship, coming on as a replacement during the win away in Argentina.

Bath said Spencer will return "later in the autumn". The club begins the 2026-27 season away at Harlequins on Friday, 25 September. Louis Hennessey, Tom de Glanville, Will Muir, Tom Dunn and Sam Underhill have all also undergone shoulder procedures this summer however will be available for the start of the campaign.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock hits opposition for six in latest sporting venture
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock showed off his cricketing skills on Northampton's tour of Sri Lanka, blasting 13 runs off just four balls as the International Rugby Stars fell short of beating a team of Sri Lankan cricket legends in a charity T20 match.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock showed off his cricketing skills on Northampton’s tour of Sri Lanka, blasting 13 runs off just four balls as the International Rugby Stars fell short of beating a team of Sri Lankan cricket legends in a charity T12 match in Colombo on Monday.

The England and Lions back-rower came in when the game was already up, with the Saints-heavy Rugby Stars team, which was led by wicket-keeper/captain David Campes, failing to chase down the 140 required to win.

Rugby.title: Blow for Bath as Ben Spencer is ruled out for start of season
Rugby.summary: The scrum-half, who led Bath to the PREM title in 2025, had an operation this summer to resolve a longstanding issue, with the club confirming he will return "later in the autumn."
Rugby.body:
Bath captain Ben Spencer will miss the opening rounds of the 2026/27 PREM Rugby season as he continues to recover from shoulder surgery. The scrum-half, who led Bath to the PREM title in 2025, had an operation this summer to resolve a longstanding issue, with the club confirming he will return “later in the autumn.”

Presumably, this means Spencer will miss the first three league fixtures at least, Harlequins (away), Exeter (home) and Northampton (away). Spencer is just one of several Bath players battling to recover from shoulder injuries, but Louie Hennessey, Will Muir, Sam Underhill, Tom Dunn and Tom de Glanville are on schedule to be fit for the new season.

Rugby.title: Singleton nearing end of rehab but leaves Gloucester
Rugby.summary: Hooker Jack Singleton is nearing the end of his rehabilitation from a cardiac incident but is leaving Gloucester.
Rugby.body:
Hooker Jack Singleton is nearing the end stage of his rehabilitation almost a year after a cardiac event during a training session; however, he will not be at Gloucester during 2026-27.

The 30-year-old has not played since the incident in September 2025 and has been receiving support from the Cherry and Whites' medical team and specialists. "Jack has followed a detailed and extensive process to reach a position where he can consider a return to full training, subject to the successful completion of his rehabilitation programme," a Gloucester statement said.

Rugby.title: Test rugby coach heads home to try and revive ailing SA rugby school
Rugby.summary: Pretoria Boys High School have recruited an old boy who has worked wonders overseas as their new director of rugby.
Rugby.body:
Pretoria Boys High School, who count 2007 World Cup-winning captain John Smit amongst their alta mater, have brought another former pupil back to South Africa to try and elevate their status in South African schoolboy rugby.

PBHS only won six of their 17 matches this season and have struggled to produce players of the quality of Smit, or their most recent Springbok, fellow hooker Chilliboy Ralepelle, and were recently ranked 43rd by South Africa’s Schoolboy Rugby Blog.

Rugby.title: Ballymore to become the new home of Australian rugby sevens
Rugby.summary: Ballymore to become the new home of Australian rugby sevens Queensland Government
Rugby.body:
Queensland has scored a massive sporting win with the Wallaroos and Australia’s Men’s and Women’s Rugby Sevens programs relocating to be based at Ballymore under a landmark new agreement with Rugby Australia.

The teams will be permanently headquartered at an upgraded Ballymore, with funding from the Games Legacy Fund powering a new high-performance facility and a brand-new Eastern Stand, transforming Ballymore into a world-class rugby precinct built to rival the best in the world.

Rugby.title: Louise McMillan: 'It just didn't quite work for my life anymore'
Rugby.summary: Louise McMillan turned down a contract from Scotland at the start of the year and has now retired from international rugby at the age of just 29.
Rugby.body:
Louise McMillan turned down a contract from Scotland at the start of the year and has now retired from international rugby at the age of just 29. The second row lost her Scotland contract in the summer of 2025 after first being awarded one in 2022. That meant she had to get a full-time job again, working in operations for an insurance company.

If she was going to be a full-time rugby player again she would have had to take a pay cut and make other sacrifices and at this point in her life, she felt it was something that didn’t feel right.

Rugby.body:
Former Australia 7s player Michael Hodge has signed a two-year deal to become Edinburgh’s new skills and contact coach. Hodge, 37, joins a coaching group spearheaded by head coach Sean Everitt, alongside Tim Sampson (attack), Brad Davis (defence) and Stevie Lawrie (forwards).

He arrives from the IRFU, where he served as Ireland Men’s U20 Assistant Coach, having previously held the role of National Elite Player Pathway and Men’s U18 Head Coach. “I’m incredibly proud to be joining Edinburgh Rugby. Moving over to Ireland has been a brilliant experience, both personally and professionally, and I’m grateful for the opportunities I had to continue developing as a coach. But this is a fantastic opportunity and one I couldn’t turn down,” said Hodge.

Rugby.title: 'On a beggar's ration, New Zealand gave Rassie Erasmus' Springboks a dig in the ribs'
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks' scrum stood up admirably as New Zealand reminded South Africa of the stark difference between winning possession and using it.
Rugby.body:
The most famous chapter in the six-part novella fought between ‘Sugar’ Ray Robinson and Jake La Motta was the epitaph in Chicago on 14th February 1951. By the 13th round the right arm of the Bronx Bull was hanging limply by his side and the Sugarman was slugging him to body and head at will. La Motta stayed on his feet, refusing to go down and taste canvas for the first time in his career, and the 1980 movie Raging Bull immortalizes the final moments in grainy back and white. A bloodied, exhausted Robert De Niro hangs on the top rope with one hand, while taunting Robinson to deliver more punishment with the other. Not for nothing has that fight passed into boxing lore as ‘The Saint Valentine’s Day Massacre’.

Over one month ago, this RugbyPass piece signalled the Greatest Rivalry series would be fought on a philosophical battleground in the no man’s land between ‘contest’ and ‘no-contest’, between winning the ball and using the ball. In recent times, progress in the game has been associated with the bulge in ball-in-play time, more phases and fewer set-pieces, and ever more try-scoring. The Nations Championship averaged over 37 minutes of ball-in-play time, nine tries and more than 200 total rucks per game.

Rugby.summary: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu pays for an indifferent showing in South Africa's series opener against New Zealand, as the fly-half drops to the Springbok bench.
Rugby.body:
Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has paid the price for an indifferent showing in South Africa's defeat by New Zealand, with the fly-half dropping to the bench for Saturday's rematch in Cape Town.

The All Blacks, revitalised under new coach Dave Rennie, ran out 33-16 winners in the series opener in Johannesburg. Feinberg-Mngomezulu was turned over five times in possession and occasionally exposed in defence, before he shifted to full-back for the Springboks in the second half of Saturday's first Test.

Rugby.body:

This goes against Erasmus’ long-held mantra that you can only play at the weekend if you can train on Monday.

Rugby.title: Jason Ryan likens All Blacks' scrum battle to '12 rounds of boxing'
Rugby.summary: Ryan, speaking to Scotty & Izzy on Sport Nation NZ, Ryan described how he saw the scrum battle from up in the coaching box at Ellis Park.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Jason Ryan has likened the scrum battle against the Springboks to “12 rounds of boxing” after escaping Johannesburg with a Test victory. Their 17-point triumph over the back-to-back World Champions had everything, from scrum penalties to cynical yellow cards; the game ebbed and flowed, culminating in an All Blacks victory in front 60-thousand at Ellis Park.

Those scrum penalties, an area the Springboks dominated for large parts of the contest, turned the result in the All Blacks’ favour late on, with Dave Rennie’s bench adding much-needed stability at scrum time.

Rugby.summary: According to Mo'unga, it hasn't taken him long to adjust to the new game-plan, and in fact, it's something the 32-year-old is excited about.
Rugby.body:

Even without featuring for the All Blacks under Rennie, the Canterbury first-five has gotten a feel for the optimism surrounding the camp on Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour of South Africa.

The last time Mo’unga pulled on the All Blacks jersey was in 2023 in France at the Rugby World Cup, a moment that will soon be in the rearview mirror. The All Blacks first-five will start in the playmaking roles alongside longtime international teammate Beauden Barrett to take on the Lions at Ellis Park on Wednesday.

Rugby.title: The Springboks' brawn was impressive, but the brains were sadly lacking
Rugby.summary: The brawn was impressive at Ellis Park, but the brains were sadly lacking and it was an incredibly untidy performance for a team that was so physically dominant.
Rugby.body:
Now that’s out of their system, you hope the All Blacks and Springboks might play some rugby. The brave team beat the dumb team at Ellis Park. You have to commend New Zealand for continuing to turn up defensively and celebrate the front row depth that enabled them to beat South Africa 33-16 in Johannesburg.

I knew Asafo Aumua could scrummage, but I feared George Bower lacked the grunt of Ethan de Groot. As it was, de Groot was the prop who had his backside handed to him by the Springboks and Bower who helped shore up a weakness that was going to cost the All Blacks this test.

Rugby.title: Grant Williams was targetted in defence by the All Blacks
Rugby.summary: New Zealand already had a recipe that worked, yet Erasmus and his team went again with Williams. For the second time, it backfired.
Rugby.body:
Springboks halfback Grant Williams was an unusual No.9 selection for South Africa. The main reason being that at Eden Park last year the All Blacks unsettled him, throwing South Africa off their game. New Zealand already had a recipe that worked, yet Erasmus and his team went again with Williams. For the second time, it backfired.

Every coach loves versatility. Williams can cover wing, which was needed in this game, but they forgot to keep the main thing the main thing. The No.9 has to be the best halfback first and foremost. If the No.9 is harassed and put under pressure, the entire cohesion of the backline or shape is out of sync.

Rugby.title: The three trouble positions which the Wallabies must resolve in Argentina
Rugby.summary: Los Pumas is the perfect litmus Test for the Wallabies, and has been so since Michael Cheika first coached the side in a Test in 2021.
Rugby.body:
Les Kiss has now named the second squad of his tenure as Wallabies head coach, reducing it from 36 to 34 players for the trip to Argentina. For the first time in 2026, no debutants have been selected in the squad, and this bodes well for consistency and for the wider group really cementing its identity.

The omission of giant lock Miles Amatosero was expected as he serves a three-match ban for his illegal hit on Japan’s captain Warner Dearns in Osaka. The unexpected omission is that of Queensland Reds’ fullback Jock Campbell, who played excellently in the Wallabies’ narrow defeat to Ireland in July.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga not the only new face in All Blacks team to play Lions
Rugby.summary: Patrick Tuipulotu will captain an overhauled All Blacks team to play the Lions in the final midweek game of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test series.
Rugby.body:
Patrick Tuipulotu will captain an overhauled All Blacks team to play the Lions in the final midweek game of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series. The headline selection, long expected since his highly anticipated return to camp, is Richie Mo’unga coming in at 10. It will be Mo’unga’s first appearance in a black jersey since the 2023 Rugby World Cup final. The playmaker will link up with Beauden Barrett, who starts at fullback, and will be backed up on the bench by Josh Jacomb.

Other new faces to the tour, Noah Hotham and Saula Ma’u, will get their first minutes in South Africa, the latter coming into the game as uncapped. Both Jamie Hannah and Ofa Tu’ungafasi are straight off the plane and onto the field after coming in as cover for Ethan de Groot and Josh Lord, who went down in Saturday’s dramatic win over the Springboks.

It will be Mo’unga’s first appearance in a black jersey since the 2023 Rugby World Cup final. The playmaker will link up with Beauden Barrett, who starts at fullback, and will be backed up on the bench by Josh Jacomb.

Other new faces to the tour, Noah Hotham and Saula Ma’u, will get their first minutes in South Africa, the latter coming into the game as uncapped. Both Jamie Hannah and Ofa Tu’ungafasi are straight off the plane and onto the field after coming in as cover for Ethan de Groot and Josh Lord, who went down in Saturday’s dramatic win over the Springboks.

Rugby.title: 'You could look at it like that': Jessie Kriel makes telling concession after Boks loss
Rugby.summary: Jesse Kriel insists the Springboks remain firmly in the fight despite their heavy Ellis Park defeat to the All Blacks...
Rugby.body:
Jesse Kriel insists the Springboks remain firmly in the fight despite their heavy Ellis Park defeat to the All Blacks, with the South Africa captain viewing the remaining three Tests of the Greatest Rivalry series as knockout rugby.

The Boks now head to Cape Town needing three consecutive victories to claim the series, but Kriel said belief remains high within the camp. “Of course, I think anything is possible in rugby,” said Kriel when asked if South Africa could still win the series 3-1.

Rugby.title: All Blacks never-say-die grit pays as Rassie sinks his own ship
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks 33-16 win over the Springboks was a classic story of weathering the storm and winning the little moments that matter.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks‘ 33-16 win over the Springboks was a classic story of weathering the storm and winning the little moments that matter. Despite their ‘dominance’, the Springboks were repelled from entries into the 22 and left coming away with zero points on multiple occasions, with the All Blacks delivering on resilience and grit to give themselves a shot in the back end of the game.

A heroic save by Jordie Barrett forced a knock-on from Malcolm Marx when the hooker looked certain to score from a rolling maul. The midfielder’s never-say-die act is no fluke.

Rugby.title: 'Walking around': Rennie questions Springbok scrumming tactic after set piece struggle
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks scrum came under immense pressure all afternoon in Johannesburg with the visitors unable to stabilise the set piece until the reserve front rowers came on.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks scrum came under immense pressure all afternoon in Johannesburg with the visitors unable to stabilise the set piece until the reserve front rowers came on. The Springboks used their strength to their advantage, looking to shove the All Blacks off the ball at every opportunity. When halfback Cam Roigard couldn’t get the ball out quickly, the All Blacks were penalised on their own feed multiple times.

South Africa flexed their advantage at scrum time but a key reversal came when the home side doubled down on scrums after winning a penalty in front of the posts, turning down points to go again with the score at 19-16.

Rugby.title: 'It was the right call': Dave Rennie weighs in on Ardie Savea's tackle on Jasper Wiese
Rugby.summary: A dramatic turning point in the All Blacks 33-16 win over the Springboks came with the All Blacks looking to land the definitive blow with a 10-point lead.
Rugby.body:
A dramatic turning point in the All Blacks 33-16 win over the Springboks came with the All Blacks looking to land the definitive blow with a 10-point lead. A Quinn Tupaea 50-22 turned the screws and had the Boks pinned deep in their 22, but a loose ball turnover ended up in the hands of Jasper Wiese. The No.8 powered through the tackle of Ardie Savea, before the All Blacks captain pinched a breakdown steal two phases later to put New Zealand back on attack.

A grubber kick from Jordie Barrett pinned the Boks on the five, where a strong counter-ruck won back possession, before reserve flanker Marco van Staden played halfback Cam Roigard, coming from a side entry to disrupt play.

Rugby.summary: Monaco Rugby Sevens Triumphs in Biarritz, Secures 2027 Supersevens Final Spot Nice-Matin
Rugby.body:
Monaco Rugby Sevens made the perfect start to its In Extenso Supersevens campaign in Biarritz, combining relentless defense with attacking flair to claim the opening tournament and book an early place in the 2027 grand final in Paris.

With the competition’s new format combining pool play and knockout matches, there is little room for error. That is especially true with only two qualifying tournaments, making the season opener in Biarritz a crucial opportunity for Monaco Rugby Sevens to get its In Extenso Supersevens campaign off to the best possible start.

Rugby.summary: "Ethan de Groot was crook overnight, and but yeah, look, we're really happy with with the effort up front, and scrum was really solid in that last 30."
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has provided his initial thoughts on his side’s important first Test victory over the Springboks at Ellis Park. The All Blacks, who trailed at half-time by one point, overcame the back-to-back World Cup winners in Johannesburg to take a 1-0 lead in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series.

Their 33-16, five-tries-to-one victory over the Springboks was built off an impressive second-half performance, despite trailing at halftime. Will Jordan’s late five-pointer sealed the deal for Rennie’s men, but the head coach was quick to cool the jets on the performance.

Rugby.title: The Springboks got drunk on their own hype
Rugby.summary: Wellington, 2025. New Zealand beaten by a record score. 43-10. Thirty-six unanswered points in the second half. A brace for Cheslin Kolbe. A masterclass from Damian Willemse. Six tries to one.
Rugby.body:
Wellington, 2025. New Zealand beaten by a record score. 43-10. Thirty-six unanswered points in the second half. A brace for Cheslin Kolbe. A masterclass from Damian Willemse. Six tries to one.

We heard about that game so often in the build-up to this Test that it began to feel like a reference point for the new Springboks. Proof that South Africa had evolved. That Tony Brown had added wit to the muscle. That the Boks could still bludgeon teams, but could now also manipulate space, shift the point of attack and unleash their backs before a defence had time to settle.

Rugby.summary: Even by Ellis Park standards, Saturday evening's Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test series opener was a raw and vicious encounter.
Rugby.body:
Even by Ellis Park standards, Saturday evening’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series opener was a raw and vicious encounter. Were it not for the feverish crowd, the sounds of bodies colliding would have been heard from the farthest reaches of the Eastern Cape.

The series opener lived up to the billing of ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’, delivering action on all fronts. The All Blacks were ahead by 10 points with 12 minutes remaining when South Africa sealed their fate with two yellow cards. One more try from the Kiwis was the cherry on top for Dave Rennie.

Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers have signed Tonga international hooker Sam Moli. The New Zealand-born forward has joined after leaving Super Rugby side Moana Pasifika after they disbanded following financial issues earlier this year.

Moli, 27, made 47 appearances in four years with Moana Pasifika and has won 27 caps for Tonga since his debut in 2021. "Sam comes and adds some quality and depth to our hooking options," said Tigers head coach Geoff Parling.

Rugby.summary: HSBC SVNS Series star Maddison Levi didn’t want her Wallaroos debut to end, having come off the bench with 30 minutes left.
Rugby.body:
HSBC SVNS Series star Maddison Levi didn’t want her Wallaroos debut to end, having come off the bench with 30 minutes left in a 67-19 defeat to the Black Ferns. “I wanted to keep playing,” Levi said post-game, having made a noticeable impact in limited time out on the field.

Levi is the all-time leading try-scorer for the Australia Women’s Sevens side, went to the Olympic Games in Tokyo and Paris, was named the 2024 World Rugby Sevens Player of the Year, and has won multiple SVNS Series events.

Desiree Miller scored in the final play of the first half, but the New Zealanders would go on to add another 33 unanswered points to their tally in the second term. It was a masterclass from start to finish for the Black Ferns, who will soon jet off to South Africa.

Rugby.title: Kyren Taumoefolau’s remarkable try-scoring NPC season continues
Rugby.summary: Tasman Mako winger Kyren Taumoefolau has already scored 10 tries in the National Provincial Championship this season.
Rugby.body:
Tasman Mako winger Kyren Taumoefolau has already scored 10 tries in the National Provincial Championship this season, backing up a historic five-try haul with another two in an emphatic 46-17 win over Southland.

Taumoefolau ran in a hat-trick against North Harbour in round one, before getting back on the scoresheet two weeks later. The 23-year-old Tongan international, who will become eligible to play for the All Blacks in October, scored five in a win over Counties Manukau.

Rugby.title: Wallaby among try-scorers as Hawke’s Bay maintain unbeaten start
Rugby.summary: Capped Wallaby Darby Lancaster scored his first provincial try in Hawke’s Bay colours on Friday evening, in a big win over Manawatu.
Rugby.body:
Capped Wallaby Darby Lancaster scored his first provincial try in Hawke’s Bay colours on Friday evening, helping the Magpies continue their unbeaten start to the NPC season with a 59-17 blitz of Manawatu at McLean Park.

Hawke’s Bay have emerged as the competition front-runners as the NPC regular season nears its halfway point, with the Napier-based outfit the last team standing with an undefeated record through four rounds.

Rugby.title: KCB dealt Driftwood Sevens blow after key player lands Monaco Rugby Sevens gig
Rugby.summary: KCB dealt Driftwood Sevens blow after key player lands Monaco Rugby Sevens gig Mozzart Sport Kenya
Rugby.body:
Reading Time: 3min | Fri. 21.08.26. | 21:01 Defending Driftwood Sevens champions KCB Rugby have suffered a major setback ahead of this weekend's tournament after their key player, Elvis Olukusi, was named in the Monaco Rugby Sevens squad for the 2026-27 In Extenso Supersevens in France.

Olukusi's selection means he will miss the fourth leg of the National Sevens Circuit in Mombasa, where KCB are chasing back-to-back Driftwood Sevens titles. The Bankers head into the tournament in buoyant mood after edging Strathmore Leos 14-12 to win the Kabeberi Sevens title last weekend.

Rugby.title: Ardie Savea: Playing the Springboks 'takes you to places where you question yourself'
Rugby.summary: Ardie Savea is back in the All Blacks camp and is "hungry to get going" after two weeks of rest, during which he watched his team begin the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour with three wins.
Rugby.body:
Ardie Savea is back in the All Blacks camp and is “hungry to get going” after two weeks of rest, during which he watched his team begin the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour with three wins.

The Kiwi captain said he hasn’t looked to assert himself on the team since joining them in Johannesburg, only looking to “add to the energy that’s already here”, happy with the momentum that’s been built in his absence.

Rugby.title: High court allows rugby brain injury case to go on
Rugby.summary: The cases of hundreds of players in rugby's multi-million-pound concussion legal battle allowed to continue after High Court ruling.
Rugby.body:
The cases of hundreds of players in rugby's multi-million-pound concussion legal battle have been allowed to continue by the High Court. A judge last month considered whether to throw out the claims due to failure to comply with an order to provide documents surrounding the neurological testing process.

Senior Master Jeremy David Cook has now allowed the legal battle, which has already stretched six years, to continue to trial after a change in lawyers representing more than 500 players from both rugby union and league.

Rugby.title: Wales great Jones returns to Ospreys as a director
Rugby.summary: Ospreys confirm former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones as a new member of their board before the 2026-27 season.
Rugby.body:
Ospreys have confirmed the return of former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones as a director. The 40-year-old has become a board member at the Swansea-based team with immediate effect.

Jones made his Ospreys debut in 2005, a year after he broke through with Swansea RFC, and helped the club to three titles and an Anglo-Welsh Cup triumph. The former lock is to return at a turbulent time amid their fight for survival under Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans to cut to three professional men's sides.

Rugby.title: Coach Stick: Why Paul de Villiers is 'the right person' to face All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Paul de Villiers will start for the Springboks in his first game against the All Blacks, stepping in for talismanic leader Siya Kolisi as the Springboks take a cautious approach to the captain's return from injury.
Rugby.body:
Paul de Villiers will start for the Springboks in his first game against the All Blacks, stepping in for talismanic leader Siya Kolisi as the Springboks take a cautious approach to the captain’s return from injury.

But De Villiers’ selection wasn’t entirely a health-based decision. Springboks coaches backed the 23-year-old’s form, allowing them to give Kolisi an extra week’s rest. De Villiers has started the Springboks’ season, his first with the team, as the starting openside flanker, and has retained that jersey in every Test since, except for South Africa’s most recent, a low-scoring win over Argentina.

Rugby.title: 'I absolutely loved it': How a 330km walk kept Rhona Lloyd on the pitch
Rugby.summary: Last year Rhona Lloyd was contemplating retiring following the Women's Rugby World Cup after falling out of love with the game.
Rugby.body:
Last year Rhona Lloyd was contemplating retiring following the Women’s Rugby World Cup after falling out of love with the game. The Scotland winger struggled after being left out of the GB sevens squad for the 2024 Paris Olympics and didn’t have time to process the omission as she went straight into that year’s WXV 2 in South Africa.

The 29-year-old needed some time away from the game before the Women’s Rugby World Cup and that came in the form of the Camino de Santiago 330km walk. “I was really not enjoying rugby and at a stage where I didn’t know if I wanted to keep playing after the World Cup,” Lloyd said.

Rugby.title: World Cup-winning duo headline 13 international re-signings at Exeter
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs have confirmed the re-signing of 13 internationals prior to the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby season.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs have confirmed the re-signing of 13 internationals prior to the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby season. This includes all five of their capped Red Roses, including Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 winners Maddie Feaunati and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, as well as Maisy Allen, Emily Robinson and Flo Robinson.

Club centurion Merry Elworthy, along with Taz Bricknell, Sofia Bekir Fuente, Lucy Nye and Sammy Wong have also signed on for more. Last season Exeter finished third in the PWR table and exited the play-offs with a defeat to eventual champions, Saracens.

Rugby.title: Uncapped Loughborough centurion added to Wales training squad
Rugby.summary: Loughborough Lightning centurion Megan Davey has been added to Sean Lynn's extended Wales training squad for the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
Loughborough Lightning centurion Megan Davey has been added to Sean Lynn’s extended Wales training squad for the WXV Global Series. The scrum-half made her Lightning debut as a 17-year-old and is the record appearance maker for Nathan Smith’s East Midlanders, having made 124 outings.

Along with Kendall Waudby [who has since joined Sale Sharks], Davey was called into Wales camp for the first time ahead of the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations. At the time Davey said: “The idea of playing for Wales was first brought to me ahead of the 2021 Rugby World Cup [held in 2022 during to the global pandemic].

Rugby.title: World Rugby ranking top-spot on the line in RGR but there is a caveat
Rugby.summary: South Africa and New Zealand not only battling for supremacy on the field but also for top spot bragging rights in the World Rugby rankings.
Rugby.body:
This weekend’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test carries added significance at Ellis Park on Saturday, with South Africa and New Zealand not only battling for supremacy on the field but also for top spot bragging rights in the World Rugby rankings.

The Springboks head into the opening Test of the four-match Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series ranked No.1 in the world on 93.96 points, holding a slender 1.68-point advantage over the second-placed All Blacks.

Rugby.title: Brett Robinson to make official 5-day visit to Rugby World Cup returnees
Rugby.summary: World Rugby chair Brett Robinson will make an official five-day visit to Zimbabwe next week as the governing body looks to build on the momentum generated by the Sables' qualification for Rugby World Cup 2027.
Rugby.body:
World Rugby chair Brett Robinson will make an official five-day visit to Zimbabwe next week, a trip the union have described as ‘truly extraordinary’. The governing body is looking to build on the momentum generated by the Sables’ qualification for Rugby World Cup 2027.

The visit also carries personal significance for Robinson, who previously played rugby in Zimbabwe before later representing the Wallabies and moving into rugby administration.

Rugby.title: Scotland's Evie Gallagher promises 'different brand of rugby' at WXV
Rugby.summary: Evie Gallagher was part of the Scotland squad that reached a record high of fifth in the World Rugby rankings two years ago.
Rugby.body:
Evie Gallagher was part of the Scotland squad that reached a record high of fifth in the World Rugby rankings two years ago and was also part of the squad that put in an excellent showing versus Wales a year ago at the Women’s Rugby World Cup in England.

And, after a frustrating one-win Guinness Women’s Six Nations campaign, the fit-again Bristol Bears No.8 believes the Scots can find that level again – and she says they will be playing “a completely different brand of rugby” during the upcoming WXV Global Series than what we saw earlier in the year.

Rugby.title: Exeter lock Zambonin to miss start of new season
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs' Italy international lock Andrea Zambonin is set to be out until the end of November following shoulder surgery.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs lock Andrea Zambonin will miss the beginning of the 2026-2027 season following surgery on a shoulder injury. The 25-year-old Italy international played 27 games in his debut season at Sandy Park, including Exeter's 26-17 defeat to Northampton in the Prem final.

Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter told the club website:, external "Unfortunately, Andrea returned from Italy's summer games with a niggling shoulder issue that, upon further inspection, was deemed serious enough to require an operation.

Rugby.title: 'It's exciting': Fijiana XV squad named for WXV Global Series Challenger
Rugby.summary: New Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker has named his WXV Global Series Challenger squad that will travel to Hong Kong China next month.
Rugby.body:
New Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker has named his WXV Global Series Challenger squad that will travel to Hong Kong China next month. Installed as head coach shortly before Fiji’s two-Test encounter with the Springbok Women, Walker has opted for consistency heading into fixtures with Spain, Hong Kong China and the Netherlands at Kai Tak Sports Ground.

Scrum-half, Kolora Lomani, continues to captain the side, who are without Adi Salaseini Railumu, Sulita Waisega and Loraini Senivutu after they were ruled out with injury. Breakout star of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, Manuqalo Komaitai, will join up with the squad in Japan, ahead of the team’s clash with the Sakura Fifteen in Fukuoka.

Rugby.title: The domestic league supplying 13 of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test players
Rugby.summary: Japan Rugby League One’s influence on the international game will be in plain sight when Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry gets underway at Ellis Park on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Japan Rugby League One’s influence on the international game will be in plain sight when Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry gets underway at Ellis Park on Saturday. When Springbok and Toyota Verblitz back-rower Pieter-Steph du Toit and Kobelco Kobe Steelers No.8 Ardie Savea lead their sides out in Johannesburg, they will be among 13 players with League One links selected across the two matchday squads.

The figure certainly speaks to how far the competition has come since its launch five years ago. A quarter of the players involved in the opening Test come from Japan’s domestic league, with another three members of the coaching teams also bringing League One connections.

Rugby.title: Rassie's tribute to Damian de Allende ahead of 100th Sprinboks Test
Rugby.summary: Damian de Allende's name will enter the hallowed halls of Springboks history once again this weekend, when the 34-year-old runs out for his 100th Test match for the team.
Rugby.body:
Damian de Allende’s name will enter the hallowed halls of Springboks history once again this weekend, when the 34-year-old runs out for his 100th Test match for the team. The bruising inside centre will become just the 10th Springboks centurion when the whistle blows at Ellis Park, with Jean de Villiers the only midfielder before him to reach the milestone.

The achievement puts even more on the line in Saturday’s historic Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series opener, in which De Allende will link up with familiar midfield partner Jesse Kriel to take on New Zealand’s Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea.

Rugby.summary: Wallaroos captain Siokapesi Palu Sekona has highlighted the impact some Australia Sevens stars have had on the side.
Rugby.body:
Wallaroos captain Siokapesi Palu Sekona has highlighted the impact some Australia Sevens stars have had on the side, who are chasing a first-ever win over the Black Ferns in an O’Reilly Cup Test this weekend.

Australia will field multiple players with HSBC SVNS Series experience on Saturday afternoon, in what will be the 100th Test in Wallaroos history. Tia Hinds and Maya Stewart feature in the starting side, while the likes of Bienne Terita and Maddison Levi will add impact off the bench.

Rugby.title: Jona Nareki on the All Blacks' new 'beast', Otago's new star and Wellington's woes
Rugby.summary: For Otago winger Jona Nareki, losing the Ranfurly Shield to Canterbury and then also to Manawatu in the same week would have been intolerable.
Rugby.body:
For Otago winger Jona Nareki, losing the Ranfurly Shield to Canterbury and then also to Manawatu in the same week would have been intolerable. But after a narrow 19-15 loss to Canterbury in Dunedin on Sunday, the prospect of a Palmerston North stumble was real. The visitors trailed 24-7 after 45 minutes and 27-12 with ten minutes left.

“I’m getting older, in rugby age only. I’m not proud of my yellow card coming in the side. I owned one for the team,” Nareki laughed with RugbyPass. “Watching the game from the sideline, I noticed we weren’t winning contact at all while Manawatu went two phases the same way then switched short side to expose us. Once we fixed that, they became easier to defend against.

Rugby.title: The All Blacks' selection policy just got a lot less sentimental
Rugby.summary: Seniority and sentiment became part and parcel of the New Zealand team under previous coaching regimes. Never mind that blokes were plainly not up to it anymore, their status seemed to guarantee them selection.
Rugby.body:
I have to say I’m relieved and optimistic. The first name I looked for, in the All Blacks’ 23 to play South Africa at Ellis Park, was Beauden Barrett. Seniority and sentiment became part and parcel of the New Zealand team under previous coaching regimes. Never mind that blokes were plainly not up to it anymore, their status seemed to guarantee them selection.

So, there’s no Beauden Barrett and no Rieko Ioane in the 23 either. Both are hugely encouraging signs that, while there’s a cast of thousands on this tour, Test caps will still have to be earned.

Rugby.title: 'Borderline Personality Disorder is my superpower'
Rugby.summary: Wales' Donna Rose tells BBC Sport how rugby union has helped her manage Borderline Personality Disorder.
Rugby.body:
Tighthead prop Donna Rose has had an unforgettable 12 months on the rugby pitch. Last year, she proudly represented Wales at her second World Cup before helping Saracens lift the Premiership Women's Rugby title in June.

From the outside looking in, she is known as a hard-hitting player with a big personality. But off the pitch, few see the daily struggles the 35-year-old copes with. Rose has borderline personality disorder (BPD), a mental health condition that causes unstable moods, behaviours and relationships.

Rugby.title: 'I've been waiting for this': Roigard on 'finally' getting another crack at Boks
Rugby.summary: Fit at long last and selected to start in his familiar No.9 jersey, Roigard says his Springboks sequel has been a long time coming.
Rugby.body:
A run of poorly timed injuries has kept Cam Roigard from lacing up his boots in the famous All Blacks v Springboks rivalry for every showdown since his debut season, with just a brief showing off the bench in his rookie year the exception. This weekend at Ellis Park, the star halfback will finally get his shot at the world champs.

Roigard’s lone showing against South Africa came in a historic defeat at Twickenham ahead of the 2023 Rugby World Cup. Then just 22 years of age, the rising star produced a brilliant solo effort try, one that saved his side from a historic goose egg.
Rugby.copy:

Rugby.summary: Waiaria Ellis is both nervous and excited about the opportunity to line up opposite one of the all-time greats in Ruahei Demant.
Rugby.body:
Waiaria Ellis is both nervous and excited about the opportunity to line up opposite one of the all-time greats in Ruahei Demant, with the teenager set for a maiden start at fly-half for the Wallaroos against the Black Ferns on Saturday.

Ellis has previously played in the outside backs for the Wallaroos, debuting for the national team as a winger against the Black Ferns in Wellington last July. But the utility back will wear the No. 10 jersey this weekend, in what will be the 100th Test in Wallaroos history.

Rugby.title: ‘Inspire the next generation’: Northland end near 50-year Shield wait
Rugby.summary: Northland have brought an end to a Ranfurly Shield drought that stretches back almost 50 years, leaving players visibly emotional at full-time.
Rugby.body:
Northland have brought an end to a Ranfurly Shield drought that stretches back almost 50 years, leaving players visibly emotional after a famous 35-12 win over Canterbury that was unforgettable in more ways than one.

It was a history-making night at One NZ Stadium for the Taniwha, who hadn’t beaten Canterbury in Christchurch since the late 1980s. All Blacks Sevens star Rob Rush shone bright as Northland ended a long-running search for the Shield as well, which dates back to the 1970s.

Rugby.title: ‘We can win this game’: Wallaroos chase historic first against Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: 30 Tests have been played between the Wallaroos and Black Ferns since September 1994, with the New Zealanders emerging victorious every time.
Rugby.body:
30 Tests have been played between the Wallaroos and Black Ferns since September 1994, with the New Zealanders emerging victorious every time. But the Aussies aren’t shying away from their shot at history, heading across the ditch with the belief “that we can win this game.”

The Wallaroos fell to a 35-point defeat in the last meeting between the rivals on April 25, in a historic Anzac Day fixture between the sides on the Sunshine Coast. Siokapesi Palu Sekona was the sole try-scorer for the Wallaroos, as the Black Ferns retained the O’Reilly Cup.

Rugby.summary: News and updates The Premier of Queensland
Rugby.body:
Queensland is the new home of Australia’s Rugby Sevens and the Wallaroos, after the Queensland Government secured their relocation to the Sunshine State as part of a mega-deal with Rugby Australia which includes a major upgrade of Ballymore and ANZAC Day Bledisloe tests.

In the latest major sporting coup by the Queensland Government, which continues to aggressively raid other states for major events, up to 90 Rugby Australia athletes and staff will move to Queensland from New South Wales to have the Sevens and Wallaroos headquartered in Queensland.
