Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus has shared his expectations of the lineout battle in this weekend's Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test series opener, highlighting the tactics and personnel both sides have that will make the contest especially competitive.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus has shared his expectations for the lineout battle in this weekend’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series opener, highlighting the tactics and personnel on both sides that will make the contest especially competitive.

Erasmus’ Springboks famously pride themselves on their set-piece, but with the All Blacks fighting fire with fire by naming two locks over the height of 203 cm in the second row and Tupou Vaa’i on the blindside flank, New Zealand are positioning themselves to be as disruptive as possible in the lineout at Ellis Park.

Rugby.title: Northampton Saints' Archie McParland set for crunch talks over club future
Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints scrum-half Archie McParland is set to have crunch talks about his future with the Gallagher Prem champions after entering the final year of his contract.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints scrum-half Archie McParland is set to have crunch talks about his future with the Gallagher Prem champions after entering the final year of his contract. Saints have started to tie down their players who are out of contract at the end of the forthcoming season and have already made England star Tommy Freeman the highest-paid winger in the league.

They are also set to meet with McParland’s Stowe School team-mate Henry Pollock’s advisors to try to thrash out a new deal that won’t be cheap, even though it is likely to fall short of the headline-grabbing £1 million that his commercial advisor, Eddie Hearn, thinks he is worth.

Rugby.title: Australia's Rugby Sevens Squads Relocate to Brisbane Ahead of 2032 Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: Australia's Rugby Sevens Squads Relocate to Brisbane Ahead of 2032 Olympic Games Fanatik
Rugby.body:
Australia's Rugby Sevens programs will relocate to a new state-of-the-art training facility at Brisbane's Ballymore Stadium complex ahead of the 2032 Olympics, the Queensland government announced on Thursday. The major infrastructure development marks a strategic shift for national rugby operations in Australia.

The new "Teams in Gold Facility" is set to be constructed as part of the broader redevelopment of Ballymore, historically recognized as the spiritual home of rugby union in Queensland. Once construction is complete, both national Sevens teams will move their base from New South Wales to their new Queensland home.

Rugby.title: 'We could have selected him': Erasmus explains Siya Kolisi decision
Rugby.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has revealed that captain Siya Kolisi was available to face the All Blacks this weekend at Ellis Park in the first match of the Greatest Rivalry series, but the coaching team opted against selecting him.
Rugby.body:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has revealed that captain Siya Kolisi was available to face the All Blacks this weekend at Ellis Park in the first match of the Greatest Rivalry series, but the coaching team opted against selecting him.

It was originally feared that the 100-cap veteran would miss a large chunk, if not all, of the highly-anticipated series after picking up a hamstring injury in the Springboks’ 17-10 victory over Argentina earlier this month. However, Erasmus gave an upbeat update earlier this week on the injury status of both Kolisi and loosehead prop Ox Nche, saying they were both in contention to face the All Blacks in Johannesburg.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.body:

Rugby.summary: Gary Teichmann has delivered a verdict that All Blacks supporters won't enjoy hearing ahead of the Test segment of the inaugural Greatest Rugby Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Gary Teichmann has delivered a verdict that All Blacks supporters won’t enjoy hearing ahead of the Test segment of the inaugural Greatest Rugby Rivalry series. The former Springbok captain, who led South Africa during New Zealand’s landmark 1996 series win on South African soil, believes Rassie Erasmus’ current world champions are primed to turn the tables 30 years on, backing the Boks to claim a dominant victory – with a caveat.

Speaking in Johannesburg at the launch of the new RGR trophy alongside former All Blacks skipper Sean Fitzpatrick, Teichmann said the memories of that painful 1996 defeat still remain fresh.

Rugby.summary: Champ Rugby champions Worcester Warriors have signed former England U20 back-row Kofi Cripps from Bristol Bears ahead of the new season.
Rugby.body:
Champ Rugby champions Worcester Warriors have signed former England U20 back-row Kofi Cripps from Bristol Bears ahead of the new season. The 23-year-old spent the past year-and-a-half at Ashton Gate, making his Gallagher PREM debut against Newcastle Red Bulls in April, but has had limited game time in the West Country.

The step down to England’s second division will see Cripps reunite with Warriors boss Matt Everard, whom he was coached by earlier in his career at Wasps. Worcester will get their title defence underway in just under a month, hosting Bedford Blues on Saturday, September 19, in what will be a repeat of last season’s final.

Rugby.title: Sana Govender: The Leinster head coach who came by way of Gdansk and Skibbereen
Rugby.summary: When Erin King and Eve Higgins lined out against Munster, earlier this month, it was for the first time as a members of Leinster’s senior squad.
Rugby.body:
When Erin King and Eve Higgins lined out against Munster, earlier this month, it was for the first time as a members of Leinster’s senior squad. It was the same case for Stacey Flood, when she started against Connacht last weekend. All three women have proudly represented Ireland in sevens and XVs, over the past few years [Flood made her senior sevens bow in 2015] yet were part of a large crop winning Leinster debuts.

The drive to get meaningful games into the four senior provinces has led to the recent prominence of the Vodafone Interprovincial Championship. The big stars missed out, last season, as they were on Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 duty, in England. For the current campaign, there have been a raft of overdue debuts.

Rugby.title: Match official appointments locked in for WXV Global Series and Challenger
Rugby.summary: French referee Aurélie Groizeleau will become the fourth female to referee 50 Test matches during the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
French referee Aurélie Groizeleau will become the fourth female to referee 50 Test matches during the WXV Global Series presented by Mitsubishi Electric. She joins Matthew Carley (England), Aimee Barrett-Theron (South Africa) and Hollie Davidson (Scotland) in reaching the landmark this year, and is the fifth French official to achieve the feat.

Groizeleau is one of 10 Emirates Match Officials appointed by World Rugby to take charge of the 30 WXV Global Series 2026 fixtures taking place across 13 counties. The 37-year-old will take charge of the opening game of the WXV Global Series campaign between England and Australia in Salford and hit her half-century the following month when she takes charge of Canada’s clash with the Red Roses in Toronto.

Rugby.title: Northland end 48-year Ranfurly Shield drought with win over Canterbury
Rugby.summary: Northland have won the Ranfurly Shield for the first time since 1979 and claimed their first win in Christchurch since the late 1980s.
Rugby.body:
Northland have won the Ranfurly Shield for the first time in 48 years and claimed their first win in Christchurch since the late 1980s, taking down Canterbury 31-12 on a history-making night for the Taniwha at One NZ Stadium.

Canterbury claimed ‘The Log of Wood’ with a nail-biting four-point win over Otago in round two before successfully defending the Shield with another hard-earned 33-28 triumph over Bay of Plenty last weekend.

Rugby.title: Who is best equipped to strike first in the Greatest Rivalry showdown?
Rugby.summary: Are the world champion Springboks or new-look All Blacks in pole position to win their hugely anticipated first Test on Saturday?
Rugby.body:
“Every battle is won or lost before it is fought”. That pithy saying by the Chinese warrior-philosopher Sun-Tzu has become an axiom of modern sport at the elite level. The winning tends to consist of the preparation: the logistics on the approach-road to battle, the detail of the planning, the precision of the fore-knowledge of the strengths and weaknesses on both sides, observed without bias.

That is the process Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie, the rival head coaches of South Africa and New Zealand, will be fine-tuning now. The battle will only be fought at 17:10 on Saturday at Ellis Park, but there are myriad is to be dotted and ts to be crossed before then – in selection, in game planning, and in physical and mental training.

Rugby.title: Ex-All Black captain Read says Argentina gave the 'blueprint' for Boks
Rugby.summary: Ex-All Black captain Kieran Read believes that Argentina provided the blueprint for beating the Springboks in Buenos Aires a fortnight ago.
Rugby.body:
Ex-All Black captain Kieran Read believes that Argentina provided the blueprint for beating the Springboks in Buenos Aires a fortnight ago. Los Pumas hosted a strong South Africa side, although missing a host of topline stars, and were able to trouble them in their 17-10 loss, missing the chance to draw level with the final play of the game.

They led 10-3 for most of the first half and created a number of opportunities out wide through a varied attacking game that implemented chips and cross-field kicks. “Even though they [South Africa] didn’t put anything on the table in Argentina, Argentina showed us exactly how we should try to beat the Springboks,” Read said on The Good, The Bad & Rugby ANZ podcast.

Rugby.title: 'Not here for a sugar hit': Waratahs expect sustained success from 'proven winner' Cheika
Rugby.summary: NSW Waratahs staff have been placed on notice to expect a rude awakening when Michael Cheika returns as coach.
Rugby.body:
From the board down to the players and his assistants, all NSW Waratahs staff have been placed on notice to expect a rude awakening when Michael Cheika returns as coach. A proven force of nature, “Cyclone Cheika” will officially arrive at Daceyville in November charged with restoring the Waratahs to the glory days after three years without a Super Rugby Pacific finals appearance and a decade of under-achieving since he left the first time.

The firebrand mentor led the Waratahs to their one and only championship in 2014, while his abrasive style has also brought success to almost every team he’s coached. Cheika also coached Leinster to European Cup glory, Argentina to the World Cup semi-finals for the first time in 2023 and, as an assistant to Trent Robinson, has helped put the Sydney Roosters on track to claiming this year’s NRL minor premiership.

Rugby.title: All Blacks and Springboks agree to drawn series scenario
Rugby.summary: The Springboks and All Blacks have agreed that in the event of a drawn series in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour, there will be no tiebreaker, leaving the series as a draw.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks and All Blacks have agreed that in the event of a drawn series in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, there will be no tiebreaker, leaving the series as a draw. Wednesday afternoon’s trophy launch event in Johannesburg revealed the decision, as former Springboks captain Gary Teichmann carried one half of the sculptural trophy through a crowd and onto the stage, followed shortly after by former All Blacks captain Sean Fitzpatrick with the other half.

Once on stage, the pair pressed the two pieces of the trophy together, revealing how magnets join them to form a single trophy, which would be handed to the winner of the series should either side claim at least three wins.

Rugby.title: Why Rassie’s next Bok generation could be the greatest ever
Rugby.summary: The Springbok dynasty doesn't look like it is going to disappear any time soon and it could, in fact, get even stronger in future
Rugby.body:
I’m positively hyperventilating about The Greatest Rivalry Test Series and it has my mind doing overtime as to how many ways it could go. It may be a heatwave here in the UK but over in South Africa, it’s piping hot for another reason. As ever, when it comes to rugby, there is no off-switch and this is what has been on my mind over the last month.

Sometimes the “next generation” can be a bit of letdown. Whether it’s people or products, the next in line doesn’t always mean an improvement. If you’ve ever spent a £1,000 on a new phone in recent years, or you’re acquainted with royal history over the past 1,000 years, you’ll know succession doesn’t always equal success — King John of England was arguably the iPhone 6 Plus of monarchs. However, the next generation of Rassie’s Springboks could arguably be the best to ever do it. They simply have to be, and for one reason: if you aren’t an almost generational-level player, you simply don’t get to play in the Test team proper.

Rugby.title: Jake White: I urge Rennie to make a huge call that won't go down well in NZ
Rugby.summary: The hours are counting down to the first Test in Johannesburg and whisper it, but the portents are shaping up well for the All Blacks. The stars are aligning.
Rugby.body:
The hours are counting down to the first Test in Johannesburg and whisper it, but the portents are shaping up well for the All Blacks. The stars are aligning. I’ll explain. If you were a rugby coach, and you were asked if you wanted to coach international rugby, the answer would be yes. Now, if you were then asked to pick any side in the world to coach most, without hesitation, would say South Africa, France, maybe England, but you can bet your bottom dollar New Zealand would be right up there. A year out from the World Cup, you’re asked where would your dream tour would be? South Africa, the year before the World Cup? Consider it done. For good measure, we’ll throw in a couple of friendlies, an extended 45-man squad and you can tour the Republic, play golf, go to game farms and have an incredible bonding opportunity. Oh, and we’ll make those warm-up games winnable and schedule the last game at altitude to replicate the first Test. Of course, you can play the Bulls. What’s not to like?

What I’m saying is Dave Rennie has nothing to complain about. It’s the perfect scenario. They are unbeaten. They have a new coach. They have renewed energy. They’ve been given the opportunity of an extended tour, playing the world champions, who are likely to be in their way in their quest to win a fourth World Cup, and they’re underdogs. They are in a helluva good place.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu leads the most shocking US Open champions ever
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu leads the most shocking US Open champions ever Lob and Smash
Tennis.body:
A New York crowd loves an underdog. Maybe that explains the unprecedented run of unexpected women’s champions at the US Open over the last 20 years. The list of recent US women’s champions includes the only qualifier ever to win a Grand Slam, the only player ever to win a major after getting into the event using a protected ranking, and the only female player to win a Slam as a wild card. The list also includes young surprises and under-the-radar veterans who rose for a last hurrah.

As the 2026 US Open gets underway, meet the five most unexpected champions in the event’s history. Who were the most surprising US Open women's champions? It might seem hard to believe now, but it wasn’t that surprising when Andreescu won the 2019 US Open as a No. 15 seed. Andreescu won the high-profile hard-court events at Indian Wells and Toronto earlier in 2019, so it made sense that she flourished on the hard courts in Flushing Meadows. She capped her title run with a convincing win against Serena Williams in the final.
Tennis.copy:
A New York crowd loves an underdog. Maybe that explains the unprecedented run of unexpected women’s champions at the US Open over the last 20 years. The list of recent US women’s champions includes the only qualifier ever to win a Grand Slam, the only player ever to win a major after getting into the event using a protected ranking, and the only female player to win a Slam as a wild card. The list also includes young surprises and under-the-radar veterans who rose for a last hurrah.

As the 2026 US Open gets underway, meet the five most unexpected champions in the event’s history. Who were the most surprising US Open women's champions? It might seem hard to believe now, but it wasn’t that surprising when Andreescu won the 2019 US Open as a No. 15 seed. Andreescu won the high-profile hard-court events at Indian Wells and Toronto earlier in 2019, so it made sense that she flourished on the hard courts in Flushing Meadows. She capped her title run with a convincing win against Serena Williams in the final.

Tennis.title: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz exit US Open mixed doubles in quarter-finals; top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka out in first round
Tennis.summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz exit US Open mixed doubles in quarter-finals; top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka out in first round Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Star pairing Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles before being beaten by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli. Williams - a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion - returned to tennis in June at the age of 44 and secured her first professional win since 2022 as she and Alcaraz beat Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and partner Erin Routliffe in their opening match.

It was also seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first match back on tour after a wrist injury sidelined the reigning men's singles champion since April. The 22-year-old was born five years after Williams won the 1998 mixed doubles title at Flushing Meadows.

Tennis.title: Retiring Wawrinka 'forever grateful' to US Open despite no wildcard
Tennis.summary: Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York.
Tennis.body:
Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York. The 41-year-old will retire at the end of year and was given a wildcard for this year's Australian Open and Wimbledon, while reaching the French Open main-draw on ranking.

He reached the third round in Melbourne and lost a pair of entertaining first-round matches in Paris and Wimbledon respectively. The US Open has received some criticism for its decision not to award a wildcard to 2016 champion Wawrinka, who did not enter qualifying despite being inside the cut-off.

Tennis.title: Vondrousova appeals to Cas against four-year ban
Tennis.summary: Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova did not let an anti-doping official enter her home to carry out a test in December 2025 and her ban is set to run until June 2030.
Tennis.body:
Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) against her four-year ban for refusing an anti-doping test. The 27-year-old was handed the ban in June after the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) charged her with denying a doping control officer entry to her home to conduct an out-of-competition test in December 2025.

Her suspension is due to end on 21 June 2030. Cas confirmed to BBC Sport that it had received the appeal but said a hearing date had not yet been set. Vondrousova, who in 2023 became the first unseeded player to win the Wimbledon women's singles title, said in April that when she refused the test she was at "breaking point after months of physical and mental stress".

Tennis.title: Why Jack Draper can take plenty of heart from seeing Arthur Fils win the Cincinnati Open
Tennis.summary: Why Jack Draper can take plenty of heart from seeing Arthur Fils win the Cincinnati Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Arthur Fils’ Cincinnati Open title was an absolute triumph for tennis, and could prove to be the moment that catapults him towards true greatness within this sport. For years now, people have been speaking about this talented Frenchman as a player more than capable of challenging the established elite, but every time he seemed to be making progress, a new physical issue would emerge.

These problems are not completely gone just yet, but this maiden Masters 1000 triumph marks a well-deserved reward for years of hard work against the odds. Many at home will have been delighted to see Arthur Fils get over the line, as seemingly one of the more well-liked players on the ATP Tour.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper and Axel Arigato Drop 'Midnight,' the Final Sneaker in Their Grand Slam Trilogy
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper and Axel Arigato Drop 'Midnight,' the Final Sneaker in Their Grand Slam Trilogy Complex
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper and Axel Arigato have unveiled “Midnight,” the final chapter in their trilogy of sneaker collaborations. Ahead of the US Open, the UK tennis star is completing the trilogy of collaborations with “Midnight,” a black take on the Dice silhouette with teal accents. Following “Dusk” and “Rise,” the new pair of sneakers celebrates the institution of night sessions. The timing of its release, on Wednesday (Aug. 26), coincides with the start of the US Open, which became the first Grand Slam to play under floodlights in 1975.

“Everything about New York feels bigger at night,” said Jack Draper of the final sneaker collaboration in the trilogy. “The city, the noise, those late sessions—it’s got that Gotham energy I’ve always loved. Midnight is the shoe for that: dark, sharp, made for after hours. It felt like the only way to finish the trilogy.”

Tennis.title: Gauff gears up for US Open with Cincinnati triumph
Tennis.summary: Coco Gauff powers past Jessica Pegula in the final of the Cincinnati Open to win her first title of 2026 just before the US Open, as Arthur Fils wins the men's event.
Tennis.body:
Coco Gauff powered past third seed Jessica Pegula in the final of the Cincinnati Open to win her first title of 2026 and make a statement before the US Open. The 22-year-old American needed only an hour and 14 minutes to defeat compatriot Pegula 6-2 6-4 as she became just the third two-time champion of the WTA 1,000 event, joining Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka.

When Gauff won the Cincinnati trophy in 2023, she went on to win her first Grand Slam title at the the US Open three weeks later. By claiming her first WTA title since winning in Wuhan last October, the two-time major winner has reinstated herself as one of the favourites at Flushing Meadows.

Tennis.title: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff beats Jessica Pegula in straight sets to clinch second Cincinnati title
Tennis.summary: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff beats Jessica Pegula in straight sets to clinch second Cincinnati title Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Coco Gauff defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula in straight sets, 6-2 6-4, to capture her second Cincinnati Open women's singles title. It means the world No 4 becomes just the third player in the Open Era, after Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka, to win multiple titles in Cincinnati.

Pegula had beaten defending champion Iga Swiatek in the semi-finals, while Gauff disposed of unseeded Sara Bejlek - who had knocked out world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka - to set up the first all-American women's final in Cincinnati for 56 years.

Tennis.title: Cincinnati Open: Arthur Fils defeats Frances Tiafoe in historic ATP Masters 1000 final between two Black players
Tennis.summary: Cincinnati Open: Arthur Fils defeats Frances Tiafoe in historic ATP Masters 1000 final between two Black players Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Frenchman Arthur Fils may have played himself into contention to win the US Open after sealing the biggest title of his career at the Cincinnati Open on Sunday. The 21st seed, who won the Barcelona Open in April, added the Cincy crown to his growing list of achievements with a topsy-turvy 6-3 1-6 6-0 victory over Frances Tiafoe in Ohio.

Fils became the third Black man to win a Masters 1000 title, joining Ben Shelton, who won the Canadian Open twice, and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who won Paris in 2008 and Canada in 2014.

Tennis.title: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula to meet in tournament's first all-American women's final in 56 years
Tennis.summary: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula to meet in tournament's first all-American women's final in 56 years Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
The Cincinnati Open will host its first all-American women's final in 56 years after Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula won their respective semi-finals. Fourth seed Gauff cruised home in her clash with Sara Bejlek, eclipsing the Czech 6-4 6-1, while third seed Pegula earned her spot by toppling defending champion Iga Swiatek 7-5 4-6 6-4.

The last Cincinnati Open final to feature two American women came in 1970 when Rosie Casals defeated Nancy Richey. Fellow American Frances Tiafoe also reached the men's final, where he will face France's Arthur Fils.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu became a victim of her own success after her historic US Open triumph
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu became a victim of her own success after her historic US Open triumph Tennisuptodate.com
Tennis.body:
qualifying as a virtual unknown and walked out as a Grand Slam champion. It remains one of the most startling runs tennis has ever seen. Raducanu won 10 matches without dropping a set, becoming the first qualifier in history to win a Grand Slam singles title. What happened afterwards has been almost the opposite: five years of coaching changes, injuries and flashes of brilliance that have never quite turned into consistency.

That contrast makes Raducanu's career difficult to define. She isn't a simple story of wasted talent, because the talent still appears regularly. Nor is she simply an injury story, even though injuries have shaped almost every season since 2021. More than anything, Raducanu's career is a case study in how difficult it can be to build a career when the biggest result arrives before the foundations are ready to support it.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper Follows Jannik Sinner’s Lead by Withdrawing From US Open
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper Follows Jannik Sinner’s Lead by Withdrawing From US Open EssentiallySports
Tennis.body:
Injuries are already tearing into the US Open, and the tournament has not even started. Less than 24 hours after Jannik Sinner pulled out, Jack Draper has followed him through the exit door. For the Brit, this one hurts even more. His withdrawal means he will go through the entire 2026 season without playing a single Grand Slam match.

Draper needs more time to recover from his injury, referring to the long-running bone bruise in his left arm, his dominant serving side, that has now plagued him for roughly 15 months. The withdrawal also marks the end of his planned mixed doubles run with Jessica Pegula, although the match-up was already uncertain as he had not received a wild card and in order to compete in the main draw he would have to go through the qualification rounds which run parallel with the mixed doubles event.

Tennis.title: Injured Sinner & Draper withdraw from US Open
Tennis.summary: World number one Jannik Sinner and Britain's Jack Draper pull out of the upcoming US Open through injury.
Tennis.body:
World number one Jannik Sinner and Britain's Jack Draper have both pulled out of the upcoming US Open through injury. Sinner has not played competitively since winning the Wimbledon title in July and is dealing with a knee problem.

The 25-year-old's decision comes a day after his great rival Carlos Alcaraz announced he was playing at Flushing Meadows following a four-month absence with a wrist injury. "Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year," said the Italian.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper ruled out of US Open
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper ruled out of US Open The Telegraph
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has pulled out of the US Open after Jannik Sinner also withdrew from the final major of the year in a bitter blow to men’s tennis. Just weeks after he wept through an entire changeover – a moment Draper would later proclaim to be “rock bottom” – it appears there will be no immediate respite from a bone bruise in his elbow that has turned into a chronic problem.

Competing at the US Open was just too great an ask for a player who has already been beset by injuries but is one of the few on tour with the tools in his arsenal to threaten the top two.

World number one Jannik Sinner and Britain's Jack Draper have both pulled out of the upcoming US Open through injury. Sinner has not played competitively since winning the Wimbledon title in July and is dealing with a knee problem.

The 25-year-old's decision comes a day after his great rival Carlos Alcaraz announced he was playing at Flushing Meadows following a four-month absence with a wrist injury. "Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year," said the Italian.

Tennis.body:

Tennis.title: US Open offers biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history
Tennis.summary: The US Open will offer the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108 million (£79.2m) on offer - marking a 20% increase on last year.
Tennis.body:
The US Open will offer the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108 million (£79.2m) on offer - marking a 20% increase on last year. The singles' champions will receive $5.5m (£4.03m) each in a 10% increase on 2025.

First-round losers will take home $140,000 (£102,667) - which is $30,000 and 27% more than last year. The prize pool includes a $2m (£1.47m) contribution to a welfare fund, which leading players have been demanding from all the Grand Slams.

Tennis.title: One month or four years? Timing key in Kyrgios ban
Tennis.summary: The severity of the ban facing Nick Kyrgios for testing positive for cocaine depends on whether he can prove he took the drug out of competition.
Tennis.body:
The severity of the ban facing Nick Kyrgios for testing positive for cocaine depends on whether he can prove he took the drug out of competition. The 2022 Wimbledon finalist tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine at June's grass court event in Mallorca, and is currently serving a mandatory provisional suspension.

The ban could theoretically stretch to four years, but it will be a maximum of three months if the Australian can satisfy investigators he took the drug out of competition. A player is deemed to be 'in competition' from the day the draws they are competing in begin until they leave the tournament after their final match.

Tennis.title: 'I feel I am imprisoning myself'
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic discusses being his own biggest doubter and the Belgrade childhood that shaped him in a new documentary.
Tennis.body:
Nobody doubts Novak Djokovic more than himself. Djokovic has won almost everything there is in tennis. No man has more Grand Slam singles titles or Masters 1,000 crowns than him. He will go down in history as one of the greatest players of all time, if not the greatest.

But even now, at the age of 39, that is not enough for the Serb. "I cannot say I feel content with what I have and who I am," he says in a new Amazon documentary. "I am always looking to be more - better, faster, stronger. Oftentimes I feel I am imprisoning myself."

Tennis.title: Sabalenka stunned by Bejlek as slump continues
Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka's preparations for her US Open title defence suffer a setback in a surprise defeat by Sara Bejlek at the Cincinnati Open.
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka's preparations for her US Open title defence suffered another blow as she crumbled in a surprise defeat by Sara Bejlek in the fourth round at the Cincinnati Open.

The Belarusian top seed was 5-1 up in a first-set tiebreak and 4-1 in front in the second set, but Czech Bejlek rallied back on both occasions to win 7-6 (9-7) 6-4. Sabalenka's position as world number one is now under threat, with Elena Rybakina - who faces Iga Swiatek in an eye-catching quarter-final on Thursday - able to replace her at the top of the rankings if she reaches the Cincinnati final.

Tennis.title: Why positive cocaine test could mean end of Kyrgios' career
Tennis.summary: Nick Kyrgios once said he did not want to play tennis into his 30s. A positive cocaine test could have brought an end to his career aged 31.
Tennis.body:
Nick Kyrgios once said there was "zero chance" he would be playing tennis into his 30s. But it was at the age of 31, while attempting another comeback from serious knee and wrist injuries, that he tested positive for a metabolite of cocaine at June's Mallorca Open.

In a post on social media, Kyrgios said it was a "huge mistake" for which he takes full responsibility. But he added that recent injuries - he has only played eight tournaments and won two matches since the start of 2023 - have taken a huge toll on him.

Golf.title: PGA Tour chief says no plans to welcome back LIV Golf defectors
Golf.summary: PGA Tour chief says no plans to welcome back LIV Golf defectors The Independent
Golf.body:
PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp offered a warning to any LIV Golf players thinking of returning to the tour that there would be no easy way back in. At the start of this year a small number of LIV players were given a path back to the PGA Tour with a three-week deadline to accept the invitation on the “returning members programme”, which was used by Brooks Koepka in January.

Koepka, who mutually ended his contract with LIV Golf when he left in late 2025, was allowed to play in PGA tournaments straight away but was ineligible to play in signature events. He also made a $5m donation to charity.

Golf.title: Tim Finchem fought for the PGA Tour. Now he’s fighting a different battle
Golf.summary: Tim Finchem, who shrewdly governed the PGA Tour for more than two decades, has been battling Alzheimer’s disease. The post Tim Finchem fought for the PGA Tour. Now he’s fighting a different battle appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Alzheimer’s disease has settled into the minds of tens of millions of people around the world, and it’s likely you’ve seen it up close in your own life. It doesn’t discriminate. Holly Finchem, in her beautiful comments to Global Golf Post about her husband, former PGA Tour commissioner Tim Finchem, made that point without even trying. Here was — here is — a man who, as people often say mindlessly, has it all: family, career, financial security, intelligence, a disciplined manner of living, good work-life balance and good health. Good health until he didn’t. Mrs. Finchem said it so powerfully: What ALS does to the body, Alzheimer’s does to the brain.

This guy had some mind. At press conferences and interviews, he ran circles around reporters, responding to our simple and direct questions with a long minute or two of gobbledygook, appearing to say everything while saying nothing, because it didn’t serve his purposes. Tim Finchem was a lawyer with a keen understanding of the nation’s capital and an uncanny ability to play things close to the vest. As the PGA Tour’s third commissioner — he had the job from the middle of 1994 to the end of 2016 — he was always playing poker.

Golf.title: PGA Tour play-off shake-up a 'big swing'
Golf.summary: Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by changing their end-of-season play-offs to matchplay.
Golf.body:
Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by introducing matchplay to their end-of-season play-offs. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp confirmed on Thursday that from 2028 the Tour Championship will be played across two weeks, at two different courses, and adopt a head-to-head format.

World number two McIlroy, who is a three-time winner of the FedEx Cup, feels the return of matchplay to the PGA Tour for the first time since 2023 shows fans have been listened to by the decision-makers.

Golf.title: The best logos in golf? A new book reveals them — and a lot more
Golf.summary: "The Best Logos in Golf," a forthcoming book on a popular topic, explores the history of logos and the clubs they represent. The post The best logos in golf? A new book reveals them — and a lot more appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
That’s not a come-on. It’s a serious question. This inquiring golfer would like to know. If you’re headed to the course, odds are you’re cloaked in something with a logo. A hat. A shirt. A belt. Golf.title: How this golfer dropped her scores from the 90s to the low 80s

She played college tennis before she ever got serious about golf, and when she came back to the game as a mid-amateur, she brought that same competitiveness with her. In just over a year and a half of real work, her scores have come down from the 90s into the low 80s, with a few rounds even lower than that. That kind of jump doesn’t happen from a swing tip or two. It happens from a plan.

Morgan Hale, the director of instruction at The Creek, has been building that plan with Anna since the start. Foundational work on posture, on club face and path through the wedges, and on structure at the top of the swing. I get folded in for what we call our “performance sessions,” where I’ll join Morgan and PGA Tour trainer Kolby Tullier to combine golf instruction and fitness in the same lesson.

Golf.title: Good Good ad and the initial response criticized by PGA Tour CEO
Golf.summary: A controversial Good Good ad and the initial response to it were criticized by PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp at this week's Tour Championship. The post Good Good ad and the initial response criticized by PGA Tour CEO appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
A controversial and since-deleted video ad for a driver developed by Good Good and Callaway Golf was “concerning,” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp says. Rolapp also said the initial response to it was “disappointing,” and that “it’s a bit of a fluid situation” in answering a question about the status of Good Good, a YouTube content group, in the Good Good Championship, a PGA Tour event set for Nov. 12-15.

Rolapp’s comments, coming Tuesday ahead of the Tour Championship, were his first publicly since the release of the ad and the fallout from it. In a portion of the video, Good Good’s Garrett Clark runs toward Alexis Miestowski, another member of Good Good, after she reaches for the club, and he pushes her. Miestowski then screams before Clark stands over her and says: “Do not touch my new driver.”

Golf.title: 'Mistakes were made': Callaway CEO apologizes for controversial Good Good ad
Golf.summary: Callaway CEO Chip Brewer apologized for his company’s role in approving a controversial ad for a Good Good collaboration. The post ‘Mistakes were made’: Callaway CEO apologizes for controversial Good Good ad appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Callaway CEO Chip Brewer apologized for his company’s role in approving a controversial ad for a driver collaboration with golf-content creators Good Good. In a statement shared on Callaway’s social channels at approximately 1 a.m. ET Tuesday, Brewer acknowledged that Callaway had green-lighted the since-deleted spot and is reviewing its internal processes to ensure that “this will never happen again.”

In the ad, Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark shoves to the ground one of his fellow creators, Alexis Miestowski, before shouting, “Do not touch my new driver.” The clip has drawn intense criticism and ignited a public-relations crisis for both brands; Callaway’s site has taken down listings for the co-branded line, which includes two driver models and balls. (As of Tuesday morning, the products were still available on Good Good’s site.)

Golf.title: Saudi Arabia will no longer fund LIV Golf. What happened?
Golf.summary: Saudi Arabia will no longer fund LIV Golf. What happened? marketplace.org
Golf.body:
The upstart pro golf organization LIV Golf hosted its last tournament of the year on Sunday, which could perhaps be its last tournament ever. LIV was financed by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. It upended the golf world back in 2022 when it lured some star players away from the PGA Tour. According to Reuters, the Saudi Public Investment Fund invested more than $5 billion in the venture. But it stopped supporting the organization at the end of this season, leaving LIV’s future in doubt.

The rise and fall of LIV Golf is not exactly an original story. A lot of other pro leagues — basketball, football, baseball — have seen upstart organizations challenge them at some point. LIV Golf fits into that tradition, said Alicia Jessop, a sport law professor at Pepperdine University, because it tried to do something different from the traditional PGA Tour.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: When taking relief from a cart path, can you choose which side?
Golf.summary: If you opt to take relief from a cart path, can you choose which side you prefer? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: When taking relief from a cart path, can you choose which side? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. We have had numerous discussions at my course on the proper way drop off from a cart path, especially on a dogleg right, with a cart path left of the fairway. A large oak is just off the path, on the right side. At a recent tournament, our opponent wanted to drop on the left side of path to have an opening to green. I informed him that he had to drop on the closest complete relief — and that was on right side, which put the shot in direct threat of the oak. He wasn’t happy…but wasn’t I correct? – Scott Hall, via email

Weren’t you just, though! The nearest point of complete relief is indeed…wait for it…the nearest point of complete relief—in this instance, from said path, regardless of whether that results in a difficult shot afterward.

Golf.title: As LIV's season (and era?) ended, 1 scene and cryptic post captured the oddness
Golf.summary: As LIV Golf's season — and potentially its era — ended on Sunday, 1 odd scene and a cryptic day-after post told the story. The post As LIV’s season (and era?) ended, 1 scene and cryptic post captured the oddness appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
It was a moment that will go down in golf history as the moment LIV Golf 1.0 — and potentially LIV Golf’s existence, period — ended. There was Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau, the breakaway league’s two biggest stars, shaking hands and embracing on the first green at The Club at Chatham Hills in Indianapolis after Sunday’s final round of the final event of LIV’s tumultuous 2026 season. Rahm and DeChambeau have come to define the story of the league’s five-year run. They were the LIV’s biggest fish — one who jumped on board immediately and the other who joined later and ultimately ended any chance of a unification between the PGA Tour and LIV.

One star was all the way in, preaching the virtues of team golf while being LIV’s biggest champion. The other dominated its tournaments but always seemed in conflict with the Faustian bargain he made to leave the PGA Tour, to which he had sworn “fealty.” In the end, as LIV stood on shaky ground after the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund announced it would pull funding after the 2026 season, DeChambeau and Rahm were the two figures holding the keys to the possibility of a LIV 2.0. Without its big-name stars, any potential investor would be unlikely to invest millions in the outfit’s next phase.

Golf.title: Gary Woodland's BMW Championship ended with an emotional (and meaningful) putt
Golf.summary: Gary Woodland's BMW Championship chances ended with a cold top, but his week still ended with an emotional and meaningful putt. The post Gary Woodland’s BMW Championship ended with an emotional (and meaningful) putt appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
All Gary Woodland could do was exhale and smile. It has been a trying few years for the 2019 U.S. Open champion, who underwent brain surgery in 2023 to remove a tumor and has been battling PTSD in the years since the operation. During an interview with Golf Channel in March, Woodland unburdened himself as he detailed how difficult it has been for him to compete on the PGA Tour while dealing with PTSD. Woodland said that going public with his diagnosis felt like lifting “1,000 pounds off his back.” Two weeks later, he won the Texas Children’s Houston Open to lift his first trophy since that Father’s Day in 2019 at Pebble Beach.

“Anybody that is struggling with something, I hope they see me and don’t give up,” a choked-up Woodland said moments after his final putt dropped in Houston. “It’s just another day, right, that I’ve got to keep healing. Today was a good day. But I’m going to keep fighting. I’ve got a big fight ahead of me and I’m going to keep going, but I’m proud of myself right now.”

Golf.title: Greg Norman ‘gutted’ by LIV Golf’s demise: ‘I would rather just see it end’
Golf.summary: Greg Norman ‘gutted’ by LIV Golf’s demise: ‘I would rather just see it end’ The Independent
Golf.body:
Greg Norman, the former controversial chief executive of LIV Golf, has admitted feeling sad over the decline of the breakaway series, stating he "would rather see it end". After investing more than $5 billion (£3.6 bn) over five years, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund has withdrawn its financial backing. Although an agreement has been reached with a private equity firm, players are encountering a scaled-back schedule and significantly smaller purses.

Having been replaced as CEO in 2025, Norman sees no long-term future for the venture he championed so aggressively throughout his full tenure in charge. "I’m sad, disappointed, gutted to be honest," he said in an interview with Skratch.

An ordinary round of golf turned into an extraordinary masterclass as an English amateur defied astronomical odds to card eight birdies across just nine holes. Allan Harrison started his round at Fairhaven Golf Club with four dropped shots down the front nine before a "pasty and a drink" at the halfway house gave him a burst of life.

The 64-year-old then fired seven consecutive birdies and eight in nine holes - a run of form rarely seen in professional golf, let alone at an amateur level. Harrison has some prowess as a former foursomes partner of Tommy Fleetwood at Southport and Ainsdale Golf Club.

Allan Harrison started his round at Fairhaven Golf Club with four dropped shots down the front nine before a "pasty and a drink" at the halfway house gave him a burst of life.

The 64-year-old then fired seven consecutive birdies and eight in nine holes - a run of form rarely seen in professional golf, let alone at an amateur level. Harrison has some prowess as a former foursomes partner of Tommy Fleetwood at Southport and Ainsdale Golf Club.

Golf.title: 'I Think There's Something Fun Coming' - Bryson DeChambeau Teases Big Things For LIV Golf 2.0

Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau remains positive about the future of LIV Golf as he teased there was "something fun coming" as the curtain came down on the 2026 season. Golf.title: Rising star Yamashita ties LPGA scoring record
Golf.summary: Rising star Miyu Yamashita ties an LPGA Tour scoring record as she surges to a dominant nine-shot victory at the CPKC Women's Open in Canada.
Golf.body:
Rising star Miyu Yamashita tied an LPGA Tour scoring record as she surged to a dominant nine-shot victory at the CPKC Women's Open in Canada. The 25-year-old from Japan made an eight-foot birdie putt on the 18th hole to complete a four-under 66 on Sunday and finish the week on a 23-under 257.

It matched Kim Sei-young 72-hole tour record lowest total, with the South Korean also carding 257 when finishing 31 under at Thornberry Creek in 2018. Yamashita broke the tournament's record of 262, set by South Korea's Ko Jin-young in 2019.

Golf.title: Is the music about to end? LIV Golf faces an uncertain future
Golf.summary: Is the music about to end? LIV Golf faces an uncertain future ESPN
Golf.body:
WESTFIELD, Ind. -- The music is stubborn and relentless, moving clumsily from rap to country to pop. At the Club at Chatham Hills, where the beat reverberates throughout the housing complex that surrounds the golf course with sameness, LIV Golf wants to convince everybody in attendance that they are guests at a party and not witnesses at a wake.

A smattering of fans sit on a small hill next to the par-3 12th tee box -- this week's "party hole," LIV's version of the 16th at the Phoenix WM Open -- sun-smacked and coated in layers of sweat. On the other side of the tee, a barricaded section labeled for holders of the "Grounds +" pass hosts no more than six people. The get-in price for the premium area was $81 at the beginning of the day, but by Thursday afternoon, it had been slashed to $53 just as Dustin Johnson stepped into the makeshift box and LIV's emcee tried his best to get the sparse crowd going.

Golf.title: The last days of LIV Golf and what the hell any of it was for
Golf.summary: The last days of LIV Golf and what the hell any of it was for Golf Digest
Golf.body:
Michael La Sasso’s final putt had barely disappeared before the champagne came out, his teammates dousing the former NCAA champion as he captured LIV Golf’s season finale in Indianapolis. The extravagance carried an uncomfortable dissonance, considering blue-collar workers were asking LIV to pay for labor already performed while millionaires emptied bottles over one another in celebration of additional millions. Still, LIV had reached a finish many doubted it would see, and La Sasso had earned his moment, even if this was almost certainly the last time anyone could spray champagne and pretend the league had a future worth toasting.

Because Sunday marked the end of LIV Golf as the sport had known it. An entity bearing the name may continue, with a schedule and teams and maybe a familiar face or two. But golf’s civil war is effectively over and what remains is worth accounting. What LIV ultimately represented and what it changed, whom it exposed and, after the billions spent and a sport fractured in two, what the hell any of this was actually for.

Golf.summary: Wyndham Clark won the 2026 BMW Championship on Sunday for his sixth career victory. Take a closer look at the clubs he used to do it. The post Wyndham Clark earns 3rd win with Ping Ally Blue Onset putter appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Like all of his other wins, Clark was dialed in with his Ping Scottsdale TEC Ally Blue Onset CB putter. He ranked 6th in the field in SG: Putting and averaged nearly 100 feet of putts made per round.

The week leading up to Clark’s U.S. Open victory in June, Clark signed a unique putter-endorsement contract with Ping to continue using the putter he first switched to in the spring. It was the first putter-only deal for Ping in more than 50 years of sponsoring Tour players.

Golf.body:
Wyndham Clark said he is "one of the best players in the world" after he survived a fightback from Rory McIlroy to win the BMW Championship in Missouri. Clark held a five-shot lead going into the final day, but saw his advantage evaporate as McIlroy drew level with seven holes left to play.

But Northern Ireland's McIlroy could not take several opportunities to move ahead, and while he closed with a bogey, Clark had a run of three birdies successive birdies as he posted a fourth-round 71 to finish the week 17 under par.

Golf.title: At the BMW, there was a cold top, mishits — and three Wyndham Clark bombs
Golf.summary: At the BMW Championship, there was a cold top, mishits — then three Wyndham Clark bombs at Bellerive Country Club. The post At the BMW, there was a cold top, mishits — and three Wyndham Clark bombs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Wyndham Clark, leading by five strokes after the third round of the BMW Championship, was asked late Saturday afternoon what it would be like to go to sleep leading by five strokes after the third round of the BMW Championship, and he talked about the “angst when you wake up.” “You wake up,” Clark said, “and you have that little pit in your stomach.”

Fun, hey? Maybe for the folks in the gallery at Bellerive Country Club, or those watching from home. They saw pros having all kinds of un-fun during Sunday’s final round. There was Gary Woodland, who’s authored one of the best stories in recent memory by playing well this year while coping with the effects of having a brain lesion. He was a stroke out of the lead on the 9th hole — then bizarrely cold-topped a drive into the water about 100 yards in front of him on his way to a double bogey.

Golf.title: The U.S. Am champ received this small but crucial feedback from his caddie
Golf.summary: U.S. Amateur champ Jack Whaley joined GOLF's Subpar podcast to talk about having his dad as caddie, his key advice and more. The post The U.S. Am champ received this small but crucial feedback from his caddie appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Jack Whaley went from trailing his U.S. Amateur final at the midway point to beating Jay Leng Jr. 4 and 3 at Merion Golf Club last Sunday. It was a special moment for the 22-year-old Englishman, but also for his dad, Andy, who caddied for him that week.

“It was phenomenal,” Jack said during the latest episode of GOLF’s Subpar podcast, where he broke down his epic week at the U.S. Amateur. “To have the opportunity to go out and do that with my dad was fantastic, and for the first time for him to caddie as well was pretty spectacular. … It’s the first time playing in such a big event and I thought it would mean a lot for him to caddie, so I asked him if he wanted to.”

Golf.body:
LIV Golf pro Harold Varner III has responded with his side of the story following an Indiana public golf course’s social media post detailing why it removed Varner and his playing partners from the course on Tuesday.

The course, Bear Slide Golf Club, is in Cicero, Ind., 10 miles from The Club at Chatham Hills, site of this week’s season-ending LIV event. According to the course’s Facebook post, Varner and his group arrived late, insisted they should be allowed to play as a six-some, later combined groups anyway, were told to leave the course and were refunded their money.

Golf.title: Bizarre rules situation sees DP World Tour pro penalized … for divot kick
Golf.summary: A bizarre rules situation sees pro Shaun Norris penalized at the DP World Tour’s Nexo Championship for a divot kick. The post Bizarre rules situation sees DP World Tour pro penalized … for divot kick appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Shaun Norris’ right-foot strike, to Norris’ credit, looked pure. Unfortunately for him, he was playing golf, not soccer. The kick, along with the bizarre rules situation that followed, came during Sunday’s final round of the DP World Tour’s Nexo Championship, while Norris readied to play his second shot on the 382-yard, par-4 5th hole at Trump International Golf Links in Aberdeenshire, Scotland. There, while tied for the lead, Norris approached his ball in the fairway, then after a few seconds, took two steps backward.

That was a no-no under rule 8.1a (3) of the rules of golf, and about an hour later, Norris’ four on the hole was changed to a six. The rule addresses playing the course as you find it, and one action that is not allowed is “removing or pressing down divots that have already been replaced or other cut turf that is already in place.”

Golf.body:
LIV Golf’s Harold Varner III was asked to leave an Indiana course earlier this week following a dispute, according to the course. Varner is playing in LIV’s season-finale event at the Club at Chatham Hills outside of Indianapolis, but some social media posts alleged that Varner was part of a group that was kicked off one of the area’s top public courses, Bear Slide Golf Club, earlier in the week. Over the weekend Bear Slide posted its side of the story on its Facebook page, alleging that Varner booked a foursome, showed up 30 minutes late, and attempted to play as a sixsome.

“We accommodated the additional group and they were informed they could go off as 2 threesomes. At the first tee, they insisted that they should be allowed to play as a 6-some. The starter informed them again that is not allowed,” the post said. “After asking the starter 4 more times, one of the group members told the starter that he was being rude and needed to calm down. Another person from the group defended the starter, saying that he wasn’t being rude and was just enforcing the rules.

Golf.title: LIV Golf should be a cautionary tale to other sports – but we won’t hold our breath
Golf.summary: LIV Golf should be a cautionary tale to other sports – but we won’t hold our breath The Irish Times
Golf.body:
Did you notice anything weird about the presentation ceremony at the World Cup final last month? Not the tragicomic sight of Gianni Infantino hustling Donald Trump offstage as Rodri and his Spanish team-mates lifted the trophy, as if Ol’ Burger Bite Face was a kind of incontinent grandpa who had wandered into a debs photo. That was weird, yes. But just the regular Trump kind of weird.

Wind the tape back a bit though, back as far as the presentation for Young Player of the Tournament to Pau Cubarsi, the 19-year-old Barcelona centre-back. The award has been on the go since the 2006 World Cup but there was something different about this go around. The camera panned to the right of the presentation party and there, in all his salt-and-pepper glory, stood Yasir Al-Rumayyan, ready to hand Cubarsi his bauble.

Golf.title: Good Good apologizes for controversial Callaway Golf video ad

Golf.body:
Good Good, a YouTube content outlet, apologized Saturday for a since-deleted video showing a man shoving a woman to the ground as part of an ad for a Callaway Golf golf club. “We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand,” the Good Good statement said. “We have since taken that content down. And sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward.”

A few hours later, a Callaway spokesperson shared the following statement with GOLF.com: “We are disappointed by the content that was posted, and are appreciative of Good Good for addressing this. We look forward to working together to ensure a more inclusive space in golf.”

On Tuesday and Wednesday, McIlroy hit on the range at Bellerive Country Club, site of this week’s BMW Championship. Across the two practice days, he hit 313 balls.

No, even six-time major winners aren’t protected from the occasional swing funk. Yes, even McIlroy has to dig himself out of it. “Yeah, I’ve definitely gotten into some bad habits in my golf swing over the past few months,” McIlroy said Wednesday during his pre-tournament press conference. “Yeah, as you play tournament golf, you start, the golf swing takes a back seat and all you’re really trying to do is hit shots and be visual and be instinctive. But as you do that, you can start to revert back into some bad habits. And I’ve certainly done that this year. …

Over the last few years, perhaps no gear trend on Tour has been as hot as the usage of high-lofted fairway woods. Pros have used 5-woods for years, but now the 7-wood has become a viable option for high-speed players and even 9-woods have their fair share of users on the PGA Tour and around the world.

In the recreational game, that’s left a lot of players asking if they too should take up the trend on the PGA Tour and trade their hybrids for high-lofted fairway woods. Early extension is a swing flaw that afflicts many recreational golfers. When the pelvis shifts toward the ball too early during the downswing, you put yourself in a difficult position to make consistent contact. That’s why it’s crucial to correct the mistake when you see it infecting your swing.

Understanding the proper technique for eliminating early extension is important, but so too is teaching your body what it feels like to swing without it. That’s where utilizing a training aid comes in handy.

Golf.body:
Lee Westwood says he doesn’t care what people think. And he said a Rory McIlroy thought “wasn’t well thought out.” Westwood’s thoughts on thoughts came Thursday, after first-round play at LIV Golf’s season-ending event in Indianapolis. Westwood and LIV teammate Laurie Canter were appearing on the post-round show of TNT Sports UK & Ireland, and Westwood had been asked whether he expected “a bit of stick” for his invite to the DP World Tour’s Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, set for early October. Westwood’s appearance will be his first on the formerly named European Tour since January 2023, and it comes after he recently paid fines levied by the DP World Tour for his play with LIV.

In response to the question, Westwood said: “I really don’t care what people think, to be perfectly honest. “I think it illustrates the fact that people like LIV players playing in their events. You know, promoters and sponsors, no matter which tour they’re on — they bring quality to tournaments.”

Golf.title: Is wrist movement ruining your putting stroke? Here's how to find out
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tom Stickney explains how your wrists should move during the putting stroke for optimal results. The post Is wrist movement ruining your putting stroke? Here’s how to find out appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The wrists are one of the most misunderstood elements of the putting stroke. Golfers are often told to keep the wrists quiet, but that does not mean they should be completely locked or rigid. The wrists are an important connection between the hands, arms and putter, and understanding their role can help create a more consistent stroke.

The first priority is understanding how the wrists influence the putter face. The lead wrist, or the wrist closest to the target, has a significant influence on how the face is delivered through impact. If the lead wrist changes dramatically during the stroke, the putter face can open or close, causing the ball to start away from the intended line. For that reason, a stable lead wrist is an important part of consistent face control.

Still it divides opinion in golf, and has split the loyalty of its champions. After the League's Saudi backers pulled its funding - having spent more than $5bn (£3.6bn) - this week's abortive season finale could be the end.

Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau is still working to help LIV Golf survive, but on Thursday he conceded that those efforts may end up being unsuccessful. The post ‘We have a lot against us’: Bryson DeChambeau gets real about LIV’s uncertain future appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau is in the hunt at LIV Golf’s final tournament of the season following a strong first round. But the leaderboard may not have been the first thing on the two-time major champion’s mind on Thursday, nor anyone else’s.

While this week’s event, LIV Golf Indianapolis, wasn’t even supposed to be the last tournament of the year, it could end up being the final LIV Golf tournament ever played. The perilous situation LIV finds itself in was not lost on DeChambeau, the league’s biggest star, following his opening round in Indianapolis. Though he struck a few hopeful notes, DeChambeau also betrayed concerns about LIV’s uncertain future, and his own, in his comments.

If you’re a confident chipper who prefers a full face of grooves on your wedge, chances are you’re a fan of TaylorMade’s Hi-Toe wedge family. These wedges are specifically designed to perform on open-face chips to give players maximum spin and versatility around the green.

These newly reimagined wedges are forged from soft carbon steel for the first time, and feature saw-milled grooves from top to bottom. Those all-important grooves are designed with ultra-tight tolerances, steeper walls and sharper radii to increase friction through impact.

Golf.title: The places golf can take you extend far beyond greens and grill rooms
Golf.summary: I wrote my first book, “The Green Road Home," 40 years ago. I didn’t know what I was doing, either as a caddie or writer, but I soaked it up. The post The places golf can take you extend far beyond greens and grill rooms appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I was 25 when I wrote “The Green Road Home,” in my parents’ house in Patchogue, on the South Shore of Long Island. On my 26th birthday a copy of it arrived there, hot off the press. That was in 1986. This piece is from a new afterword for it, a 40th anniversary edition that was published recently.

I was kind of amazed, the day that first copy showed up 40 years ago, as I didn’t know what I was doing, certainly not as a caddie, but not as a writer, either, not really. Since then, not much has changed. I’ve come to accept that as a writer and reporter my thing is to puzzle on through. For better or for worse, that’s my modus operandi, the swing thought of my professional life. Ask questions, look around, size things up, like a detective. (TV’s Lieutenant Columbo is one of my inspirations.) I don’t know what could be more fun than being a reporter.

Golf.title: McIlroy and Scheffler suffer reversal of fortunes
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy says a bit of "good work" with his team helped him rediscover his form and take the lead in the first round of the BMW Championship.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler had a reversal of fortunes that few could have predicted on Thursday's opening day of the BMW Championship in St Louis. Reigning Masters champion McIlroy, who finished 66th out of 70 at last week's St Jude Championship, was one of five players to post a six-under-par 64 at Bellerive Country Club to take the joint lead.

But world number one Scheffler, who last Sunday won the first of the PGA Tour's three no cut end-of season play-off events by eight shots, opened with a two-over-par 72. The American, who had only recorded an over par score once in his past 18 rounds, finished one shot above the worst score of the opening round and joint 44th in the 50-man field.

Golf.title: ‘Not become buffet meat’: LPGA pros are under attack by … mosquitoes
Golf.summary: The LPGA is playing the CPKC Women’s Open this week in Edmonton, Alberta, and the pros are under attack by mosquitoes. The post ‘Not become buffet meat’: LPGA pros are under attack by … mosquitoes appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Royal Mayfair Golf Club, by all accounts, deserves its first word — royal. There’s its history — it’s been around for 104 years. There’s its location — it’s in the heart of Edmonton, Alberta. There’s its golf — it’s tree-laden course has hosted men’s and women’s professional events, including this week’s LPGA stop, the CPKC Women’s Open.

Nelly Korda can certify its standing. The world’s top-ranked player said she’s found good coffee shops and restaurants. She said she’s been enjoying her time on the golf course. She’s also just been looking around. “The golf course is beautiful,” she said. “I mean, you kind of have the skyline of kind of downtown Edmonton, too, on the golf course, which is really pretty.”

Golf.title: 7 musts for becoming a better putter, according to a top teacher
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tom Stickney shares six keys to focus on to perform better on the greens and reduce three-putts. The post 7 musts for becoming a better putter, according to a top teacher appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Putting can be mistakenly considered the simplest part of golf. The stroke is short, and there is no need to generate tremendous clubhead speed. Easy, right? As any avid golfer knows, that’s hardly the case. Although the stroke is small, putting is one of the most demanding skills in the game because small changes in alignment, balance, face angle or speed can produce dramatically different results. The margin for error is incredibly slim.

That’s why the key to becoming a better putter boils down to understanding a few fundamental principles and learning to repeat them under pressure. Check out below for a rundown of some of these key fundamentals and how they work together to create a solid stroke.

Golf.body:
As Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy are battling for big bucks at this week’s 2026 BMW Championship, LIV Golf’s season finale is going down in Indianapolis after the original finale was canceled. The upstart league’s future is in serious doubt, and some of its players are readying escape plans.

Whether or not LIV’s biggest remaining stars — like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm — will be allowed to return to the PGA Tour is an open question. McIlroy provided an unforgiving opinion on the matter during his Wednesday press conference ahead of the 2026 BMW Championship. McIlroy implied that the PGA Tour didn’t need LIV’s stars to come back. He did, though, admit that he expected them to return “eventually,” but that it would (and should) be a “tough, tough road back.”

Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy was on fire in his press conference ahead of the 2026 BMW Championship, even by normal Rory McIlroy standards. Never one to hide his true feelings from reporters, the World No. 2 continued that tradition at Bellerive Country Club on Wednesday.

First, he dumped cold water on the idea that returning LIV Golf stars could improve the PGA Tour, burning them with one line: “Have they brought value to LIV?” Then, he quieted any suggestion that he should win Player of the Year honors, handed Scottie Scheffler the title early and suggested that if Scheffler kept putting as well as he did last week, McIlroy and the rest of the Tour’s stars are “F’d.”

Golf.title: How a course's unusual act of kindness resulted in a teen caddie's $125,000 tip
Golf.summary: At 14, Daniella Penaloza lost her father and her love of golf. At 17, she caddied at Old Barnwell ... and earned a $125,000 tip. The post How a course’s unusual act of kindness resulted in a teen caddie’s $125,000 tip appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
LATER THIS WEEK, the students of greater Aiken, S.C., will return to school, and the weekday caddie yard at Old Barnwell will empty. Across enormous green fairways and inside bunkers shaped like dinosaur bones, it is usually not hard to find the teens of Aiken at Old Barnwell. They lumber around the golf course like percussionists in a folk rock band — their steps thumping against the hardened earth and their bags clanking with the sweet symphony of iron against iron.

Happen upon a game at Old Barnwell and you’ll quickly realize that it is not like other private golf clubs. Happen upon a conversation with one of Old Barnwell’s caddies and you’ll find out why.

Golf.title: 'Have they brought value to LIV?' Rory McIlroy questions PGA Tour returnees
Golf.summary: Should certain LIV Golf players be let back onto the PGA Tour? At the Tour’s BMW Championship, Rory McIlroy questioned their “value.” The post ‘Have they brought value to LIV?’ Rory McIlroy questions PGA Tour returnees appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy, when asked whether certain LIV Golf players should be allowed back onto the PGA Tour, started his 22-word answer on Wednesday with a question of his own. The six-time major winner spoke one day before the Tour’s BMW Championship — and at about the same time as LIV CEO Scott O’Neil addressed the future of his league as it attempts to regroup after the loss of its primary backer, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund. The exit has led to speculation on whether LIV players would stick with the league after its season-ending event this week, or look into avenues to play on the Tour, the circuit in which most of the pros had once played.

But McIlroy questioned the point of certain LIV pros returning. “I mean, I’d argue, have they brought value to LIV? You know?” he said. “I think the PGA Tour’s in a really good spot.”

Golf.title: Tiger Woods’ $120,999,166 record is about to fall. But it's not a fair fight
Golf.summary: Scottie Scheffler’s pursuit of Tiger Woods' career-earnings haul is a hot topic this week. But the chase needs to be kept in perspective. The post Tiger Woods’ $120,999,166 record is about to fall. But it’s not a fair fight appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When Scottie Scheffler tells you he’s a rich man, he’s not talking about his bank account. He’s referring to his family: high-school-sweetheart-turned-wife Meredith and their towheaded sons, Bennett (2) and Remy (5 months). He’s referring to his faith (he’s a devout Christian and regular at Park Cities Presbyterian Church in Dallas). And, in a distant third among his soul-fillers, he’s referring to his golf (though not in the name of chasing titles or history or fame; Scheffler is driven by the singular pursuit of executing each shot and each task as it comes — with as much care, skill and focus as his body and mind will allow).

None of which to say that the guy hasn’t also banked a Brink’s truck or two full of cash. Scheffler’s career windfall has come into focus this week as he prepares for the second of three legs of the PGA Tour’s FedEx Cup playoffs, the BMW Championship, because he is on the cusp of a seemingly momentous achievement: usurping Tiger Woods as the Tour’s all-time leading money earner. Scheffler ($119,964,411) trails Woods ($120,999,166) by “only” $1,034,755, meaning if he finishes in a three-way tie for third or better at Bellerive Country Club in St. Louis, Scheffler will assume the gilded throne. After Scheffler’s exemplary form in Memphis last week, where he won by a touchdown and a two-point conversion, smart money says Woods’ record will fall this week.

Golf.title: 8 things LIV’s CEO told reporters at season finale — and what they mean
Golf.summary: LIV Golf's CEO Scott O'Neil spoke to reporters for likely the final time in 2026. Here's what he said and what it means. The post 8 things LIV’s CEO told reporters at season finale — and what they mean appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
WESTFIELD, Ind. — For the second time in two weeks and perhaps the last time in quite a while, LIV CEO Scott O’Neil sat in front of cameras and reporters (and many interested LIV staffers) for a proper, professional press conference.

It lasted 33 minutes. It was nearly 4,000 words long. And there were some clues into LIV’s present and its future, among plenty of veiled coach-speak, CEO-speak, leader-speak. I’m here to parse through it on your behalf, like Trent Crimm of the Independent, aka the fictitious reporter from “Ted Lasso” — whom O’Neil himself likened me to during the proceedings.

Golf.title: Jack Whaley revisits the crucial shots from his U.S. Amateur win
Golf.summary: On this week's episode of Subpar, newly-minted U.S. Amateur champion Jack Whaley revisited the crucial shots from his winning week. The post Jack Whaley revisits the crucial shots from his U.S. Amateur win appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Like the U.S. Open, hopefuls must first qualify to gain entry into the tournament, either by their WAGR ranking or by going through local and final qualifying. Once there, 36 holes of stroke play determine which 64 of the 312 players in the field will move on to the match-play portion of the championship. This year, 16 players battled for the 11 remaining match-play spots at the end of the stroke-play portion of the championship.

Among those 11 players who got through was Jack Whaley, who became the newly-minted U.S. Amateur champion shortly thereafter. After punching his ticket to the Round of 64, Whaley had to defeat six consecutive opponents in order to claim the title.

Golf.summary: GOLF contributor Shaun Tolson's recent trip to Virginia proved that the golf-rich state is indeed for lovers — food lovers, that is. The post From bison ribeyes to melon gazpacho, these are Virginia’s can’t-miss bites appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As a writer who traverses the globe covering golf, travel and all things food and beverage — and who racked up 110,000 frequent-flyer miles in 2025 — GOLF contributor Shaun Tolson has visited some of the world’s most famous golf clubs, resorts and best-kept secrets. Below, in Clubhouse Eats, he shares some of his favorite bites and sips from his recent travels.

It’s been more than 50 years since the advertising firm The Martin Agency (then Martin & Woltz Inc.) created the famous slogan “Virginia is for Lovers.” At the time, the slogan’s intention was to attract younger travelers to the state’s beaches, historical sites, and areas for outdoor adventure. But based on a few of my recent visits to Old Dominion — as the state is sometimes called — it’s clear Virginia is for food lovers, too.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy just hit LIV Golf with a brutal parting shot
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy just hit LIV Golf with a brutal parting shot Golf Digest
Golf.body:
Despite reports last week that LIV Golf had secured an angel investor for 2027, the league’s slow-motion collpase has continued unabated. The season-ending team championship was finally canceled, reports of countless unpaid vendors and employees began to surface, and persistent, albeit unsubstantiated, rumors that Jon Rahm’s LIV days were numbered continued to swirl. What happens next is anyone’s guess, but one thing is clear:

LIV Golf, as it has existed the past five years, is dead. It's said that you're not supposed to beat a dead horse, but after his pro-am appearance on Wednesday at the BMW Championship, Rory McIlroy—long one of LIV Golf's most outspoken critics—hit the floundering league with one last roundhouse for the road. Take it away, Rors.
